entries.subject: types: fix the behavior of casting json string to integers (#48010)
modules: pkg/executor / sessionctx flags (AllowNegativeToUnsigned gating in write statements)
entries.what: JSON-string -> UNSIGNED integer conversion ignores `AllowNegativeToUnsigned` in write contexts and can silently wrap negatives to huge values (bypassing strict-mode overflow handling) because the JSON-string branch returns a negative `int64` that is later cast to `uint64` without range/flag checks.
entries.impact: Data consistency risk: in INSERT/UPDATE/DDL/LOAD contexts where negative->unsigned should overflow/clip (or error in strict mode), JSON strings like `"-1"` can silently become `18446744073709551615` (BIGINT UNSIGNED) or other out-of-range values without any overflow error, because the conversion returns `err==nil` and bypasses `AllowNegativeToUnsigned` gating. This can corrupt stored values and violate MySQL/TiDB semantics for write statements.
entries.fix: In `ConvertJSONToInt` JSON-string branch, (1) `trim := strings.TrimSpace(str)` before sign checks, and (2) when `unsigned==true`, convert using a path that respects `sc.TypeFlags().AllowNegativeToUnsigned()` and bounds (e.g., parse to `int64` then call `ConvertIntToUint(sc.TypeFlags(), parsed, IntegerUnsignedUpperBound(tp), tp)` and return `int64(u)`), instead of returning a negative `int64` that is later blindly cast to `uint64` in `Datum.convertToUint`. Consider also clamping JSON-string results to `tp` bounds inside `ConvertJSONToInt` to match other JSON numeric type branches.
entries.verify: SQL-level: (1) `create table tu(a bigint unsigned); set sql_mode='STRICT_TRANS_TABLES'; insert into tu values (cast('"-1"' as json));` should error (or at least not store max-uint); (2) same with `set sql_mode=''` should clip to 0 with warning; (3) SELECT cast behavior remains: `select cast(cast('"-1"' as json) as unsigned)` returns `18446744073709551615` and `... as signed` returns `-1`. Add/extend integration tests to cover INSERT into unsigned integer columns from JSON-string negatives.
entries.evidence: New behavior in `pkg/types/convert.go:631-643` routes JSON strings by `isNegative := len(str) > 1 && str[0] == '-'` and uses `StrToInt` for negative strings regardless of `unsigned` and without consulting `sc.TypeFlags().AllowNegativeToUnsigned()`; `pkg/types/datum.go:1243-1246` then does `i64, err = ConvertJSONToInt(sc, j, true, tp); val = uint64(i64)` (no bounds/flag handling). Insert/update contexts explicitly disable negative->unsigned (`pkg/executor/executor.go:2166-2173` sets `WithAllowNegativeToUnsigned(false)`), and numeric JSON paths respect it via `ConvertIntToUint(sc.TypeFlags(), ...)` (`pkg/types/convert.go:600-602`). Regression confirmed vs first parent: `a565692...:pkg/types/convert.go:631-638` used `StrToUint` when `unsigned==true`, so `"-1"` produced overflow->0 (+err) rather than `-1` -> `uint64(-1)`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `pkg/types/convert.go` still uses the same untrimmed `isNegative := len(str) > 1 && str[0] == '-'` logic for JSON strings, and `pkg/types/datum.go` still converts JSON->uint via `val = uint64(i64)` after `ConvertJSONToInt(...)`; no later fix found.

entries.subject: parser, planner: fix embedded setOprStmt will be seen as SetOprSelectList item and lost its orderBy and Limit (#49421)
entries.what: Planner regression: `buildSetOpr()` breaks INTERSECT-precedence grouping when encountering a `*ast.SetOprSelectList` that has embedded `OrderBy/Limit`, which can cause the INTERSECT operator to be misrouted into the UNION/EXCEPT stage and executed as UNION (distinct) instead of INTERSECT.
entries.impact: Queries that use `INTERSECT` with an operand that is an embedded set-op statement carrying its own `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` (e.g. `A INTERSECT (B UNION C ORDER BY ... LIMIT ...)`) can be planned/executed with UNION semantics instead of INTERSECT, producing wrong results (SQL semantics/correctness regression).
entries.fix: In `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go` remove the `if x.Limit != nil || x.OrderBy != nil { breakIteration = true }` guard inside the INTERSECT-precedence grouping loop (so `INTERSECT` always groups across `*ast.SetOprSelectList` operands regardless of embedded `OrderBy/Limit`). If a barrier is still desired, then `buildExcept/buildUnion` must be extended to handle `afterSetOpts[i]==INTERSECT`, but the minimal correct fix is to not break the INTERSECT grouping here.
entries.verify: Add executor+planner tests for INTERSECT with embedded set-op + order/limit, e.g. `select 1 intersect ((select 1 union select 2 order by 1 desc limit 1))` should return empty; and a variant where inner topN returns `1` should return `1`. Also add a plan test to ensure the top-level operator remains INTERSECT (not UNION).
entries.evidence:
- `pkg/parser/parser.y:10247` sets `nextSetOprList.AfterSetOperator = $2` while also copying `limit2/orderBy2` from embedded `*ast.SetOprStmt`, so a `*ast.SetOprSelectList` with non-nil `Limit/OrderBy` can legally have `AfterSetOperator=INTERSECT`.
- `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:2070` breaks INTERSECT grouping when `selects[i+1]` is `*ast.SetOprSelectList` with `Limit/OrderBy` (sets `breakIteration=true` at `:2081`). This can create an intersect-segment whose *first* node has `AfterSetOperator=INTERSECT`.
- `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:2227` `buildExcept()` treats any `afterSetOpts[i]` that is not `EXCEPT/EXCEPT ALL` as UNION input (`else` branch at `:2250`), and `divideUnionSelectPlans()` treats any non-`UNION ALL` as DISTINCT (`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:2300`). So an `INTERSECT` operator leaking into `afterSetOpts` will be planned as UNION (distinct).

entries.subject: expression: pass const bool to all calls for expression.ConstItem (#49756)
entries.what: `APPROX_PERCENTILE` percent constness was loosened to `ConstItem(false)` in TypeInfer, allowing parameter-dependent percent values under prepared plan cache. Because percent range validation only happens during TypeInfer (not on cached-plan reuse), later executions with different `?` can bypass the range check and feed invalid `percent` into executor percentile selection, potentially causing a panic (`percent <= 0`) or wrong semantics (`percent > 100`).
entries.impact:
- Correctness/compatibility: a cached prepared statement using `APPROX_PERCENTILE(col, ?)` can bypass the percent range check on cache hits when `?` changes later.
- Stability: `percent <= 0` can drive `k <= 0` into `selection.Select`, leading to a possible panic (process crash / DoS) instead of returning a SQL error.
- Semantics: `percent > 100` would silently clamp to 100th percentile on cache hit, contradicting the planner-time “out of range” error.
entries.fix:
Pick one:
1) Re-validate `percent` on every execution (executor side): add a range guard in `buildApproxPercentile` (or before calling `selection.Select`) so `percent` outside `[1,100]` returns a proper SQL error instead of reaching `selection.Select`.
2) If runtime validation is not feasible, make the statement uncacheable for prepared plan cache when the percent argument is not strict-constant across contexts (i.e., depends on params), so TypeInfer runs each execution and the existing range check remains effective.
entries.verify:
Manual SQL repro (prepared plan cache enabled):
1) `set tidb_enable_prepared_plan_cache=ON;`
2) `prepare s from 'select approx_percentile(a, ?) from t';`
3) `set @p=50; execute s using @p;` (populate cache)
4) `set @p=0; execute s using @p;` (should return “out of range” error; must not panic)
Also check `select @@last_plan_from_cache;` to confirm step (4) is a cache hit (or verify plan-cache skip behavior if you choose fix #2).
entries.evidence:
- pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:143: `typeInfer4ApproxPercentile` now uses `a.Args[1].ConstItem(false)` and does *all* percent validation (`percent <= 0 || percent > 100`) only during TypeInfer (planner-time).
- pkg/expression/util.go:1166: `ParamMarkerExpression` sets `Constant.ParamMarker` when `StmtCtx.UseCache` is true (prepared plan cache enabled), meaning the cached plan’s percent expression can evaluate to *different* values across executions while still being `ConstItem(false)`.
- pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:166: `StmtCtx.UseCache` is set before plan generation; pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:352 shows cache-hit handling only calls `RebuildPlan4CachedPlan` which only runs `rebuildRange` (no re-TypeInfer / no re-validation of aggregate args).
- pkg/executor/aggfuncs/builder.go:147: `buildApproxPercentile` re-evaluates `aggFuncDesc.Args[1]` each execution but does not re-check range; it relies on the comment “Checked while building descriptor”.
- pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_percentile.go:41: `percentile()` computes `k := ceil(len * percent/100)` and only clamps `k > len`; for `percent <= 0`, `k <= 0` flows into pkg/util/selection/selection.go:26 (`Select(..., k)`), which passes `k-1` to `introselect`; pkg/util/selection/selection.go:84 (`randomPivot`) can panic when recursion reaches `right < left` (mod by `right-left+1 == 0`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to upstream/master (b75374faa6): `buildApproxPercentile` still does not validate the percent range, and `selection.Select` still assumes `k >= 1`; no later fix found for this specific plan-cache bypass.

entries.subject: planner: remove the limitation that predicates can't be pushed through `Projection` on `TableDual` (#51329)
entries.what: Predicate pushdown through `Projection` on `TableDual` can change SQL semantics for mutable/non-deterministic projection expressions by evaluating them twice (once for the pushed-down filter, once for the projection output), so the returned values can violate the original predicate and/or side effects can execute extra times.
entries.impact: Wrong results and/or duplicated side effects for derived tables/constant subqueries built on `TableDual` when outer predicates reference projection outputs computed by mutable functions (e.g. `rand()`, `uuid()`, `sleep()`): rows may be returned whose output values do not satisfy the predicate, and side-effectful expressions may run multiple times.
entries.fix: In `LogicalProjection.PredicatePushDown`, do not push a substituted predicate through the projection if the substituted predicate contains mutable/side-effect functions (e.g. gate on `!expression.IsMutableEffectsExpr(newFilter)` in addition to the existing `HasGetSetVarFunc` check), at least for the `Projection -> TableDual` case. Keep such predicates above the projection to ensure the output value matches the value used for filtering; still allow pushing pure/immutable predicates so #50614-style constant folding works.
entries.verify: Add a deterministic regression test using a fixed seed: run `select r from (select rand(1202) as r) t where r > 0.5;` and assert the returned `r` is `> 0.5` (it should be `0.87531795899879` per `MysqlRng.Gen()`); without the guard, this can return `0.001273...` and fail.
entries.evidence: This commit removes the `LogicalTableDual` early-return in `LogicalProjection.PredicatePushDown`, so predicates are always rewritten via `ColumnSubstituteImpl` and pushed down (`pkg/planner/core/rule_predicate_push_down.go:516`). Pushdown inserts a `LogicalSelection` below the `LogicalProjection` (`pkg/planner/core/rule_predicate_push_down.go:76`), and `LogicalTableDual.PredicatePushDown` does not consume predicates (`pkg/planner/core/rule_predicate_push_down.go:148`), so the substituted expression is evaluated in Selection and then evaluated again in Projection. Execution-wise, Selection evaluates filters via `expression.EvalBool` (`pkg/executor/executor.go:1635`) while Projection evaluates its `Exprs` separately. This is unsafe for mutable/non-deterministic funcs: `ast.Rand`, `ast.UUID`, `ast.Sleep` etc are explicitly classified as mutable-effects (`pkg/expression/function_traits.go:213`), and `RAND()` advances the RNG on every eval (`pkg/expression/builtin_math.go:1070`, `pkg/util/mathutil/rand.go:49`). Deterministic demonstration: for `RAND(1202)`, the first `Gen()` is `0.87531795899879` and the second is `0.0012732660409745444`, so after pushdown `select * from (select rand(1202) as r) t where r > 0.5;` can return `r=0.00127...` (predicate evaluated on the first call, output produced by the second).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed in later history: `upstream/master` still rewrites/pushes predicates through projection via `ColumnSubstituteImpl` without a mutable-effects guard (`pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_projection.go:93`, `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_projection.go:643`).

entries.subject: planner: choose to generate optimal plans without plan cache rather than generating suboptimal plans and caching it when generating MVIndex plans (#51546)
entries.what: Planner can panic when extracting JSON array elements for MVIndex planning because `IsImmutableFunc` is too permissive (treats `*Column` etc as “immutable”), leading to `EvalJSON(..., chunk.Row{})` on row-dependent expressions.
entries.impact: Blocker correctness/runtime risk: optimizer can panic while generating MVIndex plans for queries that match MV index predicates but use a non-constant RHS for `json_contains/json_overlaps` (e.g. column, correlated column, or function over a column). This can crash the query (and possibly the server if panic isn’t fully contained) instead of cleanly deciding “cannot use MVIndex”.
entries.fix: Make the “safe to Eval* with `chunk.Row{}`” predicate reject row-dependent expressions. Minimal fix: change `IsImmutableFunc` to return `true` only for `*Constant` and for foldable `*ScalarFunction` whose args are also `IsImmutableFunc`, and return `false` for other expression kinds (at least `*Column`, `*CorrelatedColumn`, subquery expressions, etc.). Alternatively, keep `IsInmutableExpr`-style default `false` and add a `*Constant` case that returns `true` even when `ParamMarker/DeferredExpr` exist (plan-cache skipping is already handled separately).
entries.verify: Add a planner regression test (or manual SQL repro) with an MVIndex table and a predicate like `json_contains(mv_json_col, other_json_col)` / `json_overlaps(mv_json_col, other_json_col)`; ensure optimization does not panic and simply declines MVIndex path construction. Also cover `cast(other_col as json)` and correlated-column variants.
entries.evidence: `expression.IsImmutableFunc` returns true for any non-`*ScalarFunction` (default branch) (`pkg/expression/util.go:1353-1370`). `buildPartialPaths4MVIndex` passes `sf.GetArgs()[1]` / `sf.GetArgs()[1-jsonPathIdx]` into `jsonArrayExpr2Exprs` for `json_contains/json_overlaps` without restricting it to constants (`pkg/planner/core/indexmerge_path.go:1308-1327`). `jsonArrayExpr2Exprs` then calls `jsonArrayExpr.EvalJSON(..., chunk.Row{})` after the permissive `IsImmutableFunc` check (`pkg/planner/core/indexmerge_path.go:1647-1652`). If that argument is a `*expression.Column` (e.g. `json_contains(mvcol, other_json_col)`), `Column.EvalJSON` calls `row.IsNull` (`pkg/expression/column.go:499-503`), and `chunk.Row.IsNull` dereferences `r.c` (`pkg/util/chunk/row.go:221-222`), which panics for `chunk.Row{}`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (ref `b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`): `pkg/expression/util.go` still has `IsImmutableFunc` defaulting to `true` for non-`*ScalarFunction`, and `pkg/planner/core/indexmerge_path.go` still evaluates `jsonArrayExpr.EvalJSON(..., chunk.Row{})` guarded only by `IsImmutableFunc` (no additional column/subquery guard). No fix found in `git log 54cca35..upstream/master -- pkg/expression/util.go pkg/planner/core/indexmerge_path.go`.

entries.subject: util: skip always false DNF (#51901)
entries.what: Prepared plan cache unsoundness: skipping empty-range DNF items can prune parameter-dependent OR branches from `AccessCondition` without setting `SkipPlanCache`, so a cached plan may later return incomplete/incorrect results when parameters change.
entries.impact: Potential wrong results under prepared plan cache: an OR-branch that is empty for the first execution’s parameter values can be dropped from `AccessCondition`, then subsequent `EXECUTE` with different parameters can miss rows (or return empty) because the cached plan no longer contains that OR-branch at all.
entries.fix: When skipping a DNF item due to empty ranges, if plan cache is enabled and the skipped item contains mutable constants (`ParamMarker`/`DeferredExpr`), call `StmtCtx.SetSkipPlanCache(...)` before `continue`. Alternative: keep the original OR predicate as a residual filter (`hasResidual=true` / push full DNF into `RemainedConds`) so cached plans don’t structurally depend on current parameter values.
entries.verify: Repro with prepared plan cache enabled: create `t(a int, index idx(a))`; `prepare s from 'select /*+ use_index(t, idx) */ * from t where (a > ? and a < ?) or (a = 10)'`; first `execute s using @x=1,@y=2` (interval empty) then `execute s using @x=1,@y=100`; check `select @@last_plan_from_cache` and compare rowcounts—cached plan should not drop the first OR-branch when params change.
entries.evidence: `pkg/util/ranger/detacher.go:739` skips a DNF branch when `len(res.Ranges)==0`, so that OR-branch is removed from `newAccessItems` and thus from the resulting `AccessCondition`. With prepared plan cache, parameter values are read via `Constant.getLazyDatum` (`pkg/expression/constant.go:234`), so “empty range” can be parameter-dependent. The pruned `path.AccessConds` becomes the scan `AccessCondition` (`pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go:2789`) and is what plan-cache rebuild uses (`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:726`), so omitted OR-branches cannot reappear on later executions. Plan-cache skipping for TableDual only checks mutable consts in `path.AccessConds` (`pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go:1411`, `pkg/expression/util.go:1466`), which can miss pruned branches entirely.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` and the same `len(ranges)==0 { continue }` logic remains in `pkg/util/ranger/detacher.go` without an added plan-cache guard; planner still bases TableDual uncache decision on `path.AccessConds` only.

entries.subject: statistics: concurrency init stats (#51403)
entries.what: `performance.enable-stats-cache-mem-quota=false` selects a map-backed stats cache that is not safe for concurrent writes; with `performance.concurrently-init-stats=true` (default in this commit), init-stats spawns multiple goroutines that call `StatsCache.Put` concurrently, which can trigger `fatal error: concurrent map writes` during bootstrap.
entries.impact: TiDB can crash (panic) during bootstrap/init-stats for deployments that set `performance.enable-stats-cache-mem-quota=false` while concurrent init-stats is enabled (this PR also defaults concurrent init-stats to true), turning a previously working config into a startup failure.
entries.fix: Make the non-quota stats cache implementation safe under concurrent `Put`/`Del` (e.g., add a mutex or switch to a concurrent map), or force init-stats to run with concurrency=1 / the non-concurrent path when `Performance.EnableStatsCacheMemQuota` is false, or always use the LFU stats cache implementation for init-stats regardless of the mem-quota toggle.
entries.verify: Start TiDB with `enable-stats-cache-mem-quota=false` and concurrent init-stats enabled (or on newer code where it’s always enabled); ensure bootstrap/init-stats completes without `fatal error: concurrent map writes` and logs indicate stats init completion.
entries.evidence: `pkg/statistics/handle/initstats/load_stats.go`: `LoadStats` starts `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0)` goroutines; each runs `ls.dealFunc(...)` concurrently. `pkg/statistics/handle/bootstrap.go`: concurrency branches use `initstats.NewWorker(rc.Next, ...)` for meta/hist/topn/buckets; the deal funcs call `cache.Put(...)`. `pkg/statistics/handle/cache/statscacheinner.go`: when `Performance.EnableStatsCacheMemQuota` is false, `NewStatsCache()` picks `mapcache.NewMapCache()`. `pkg/statistics/handle/cache/internal/mapcache/map_cache.go`: `MapCache` is backed by a plain Go `map` and `Put` mutates it without synchronization.
entries.later_fix_evidence: On `upstream/master`, `pkg/statistics/handle/cache/statscacheinner.go` still selects `mapcache.NewMapCache()` when mem-quota is disabled and `pkg/statistics/handle/cache/internal/mapcache/map_cache.go` remains an unsynchronized map. Concurrent init-stats is now always enabled after #60408, and the init-stats worker (`pkg/statistics/handle/initstats/load_stats_page.go`) still spawns multiple goroutines, so the same `concurrent map writes` panic risk remains for `enable-stats-cache-mem-quota=false`.

entries.subject: planner: fix the wrong result caused by `year_col cmp out-of-range-uint` (#53395)
entries.what: YEAR range building change can make `YEAR_col >= out-of-range-uint64` return wrong results: the new cap-to-`MaxInt64` avoids overflow but, for `>=`, leads to a clamped YEAR constant (2155) with no operator tightening, yielding range `[2155,+inf)` while the executor comparison against the real unsigned constant is always false.
entries.impact: Potential wrong results: `YEAR_col >= <out-of-range-uint64>` (or `<out-of-range-uint64> <= YEAR_col`) can produce a non-empty index range starting at 2155 and return rows with YEAR=2155 even though the executor-level predicate is unsatisfiable; affects primary key / index access conditions where the predicate is detached and not rechecked.
entries.fix: In `refineValueAndOp` YEAR handling, when `ErrWarnDataOutOfRange` and the converted YEAR value differs from `preValue`, also refine inclusive ops to keep ranges exact: if `op==ast.GE` and `value.GetInt64() < preValue` then set `op=ast.GT`; if `op==ast.LE` and `value.GetInt64() > preValue` then set `op=ast.LT`. Add regression tests covering `YEAR >= <out-of-range-uint64>` with an existing 2155 row (expect empty).
entries.verify: Add a planner/executor test: create `year` PK with a 2155 row and run `select * from t where y >= 16212511333665770580` (expect empty); also verify `<`/`<=` cases still return all rows (e.g. the new `TestIssue50235`) and that the access condition is not retained as a filter in the plan/explain for the GE case.
entries.evidence: Range build: `pkg/util/ranger/points.go:332-363` caps `KindUint64>MaxInt64` to `MaxInt64`, then `ConvertToMysqlYear()` clamps to 2155 and for `ast.GE` clears error without tightening the op; GE range construction is `[value,+inf]` at `pkg/util/ranger/points.go:456-459`. Runtime compare: YEAR-vs-INT refining only applies when `AdjustYear(... )` returns nil (`pkg/expression/builtin_compare.go:1639-1652`), so out-of-range uint64 (GetInt64() wraps negative) is not adjusted; comparison uses unsigned flags (`pkg/expression/builtin_compare.go:2862-2880`, `pkg/types/compare.go:90-110`) making `year_val >= huge_uint` always false. Access conds are not reserved as filters for YEAR comparisons (e.g. `filterConds: []` in `pkg/util/ranger/ranger_test.go:937-963`), so an over-wide GE range can leak extra rows.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `remotes/upstream/master`; `remotes/upstream/master:pkg/util/ranger/points.go` still contains the same out-of-range uint64 capping and the `case ast.GE, ast.LE: err = nil` handling (no GE->GT / LE->LT tightening), so this is not fixed later.

entries.subject: planner: fix small regression caused by #53094 (#53646)
entries.what: PointGet plan-cache hit path skips `checkPreparedPriv` (privilege + table-lock checks) once a cached PointGet executor exists (`stmt.PointGet.Executor != nil`), enabling prepared EXECUTE to proceed without runtime privilege/table-lock enforcement on cache hits.
entries.impact: Prepared EXECUTE statements that hit the session plan cache via PointGet short path can bypass runtime privilege recheck and table-lock checks after privileges/locks change (e.g., REVOKE in another session), leading to unauthorized visibility or lock-rule violations.
entries.fix: Do not skip `checkPreparedPriv` for PointGet cache hits (always run it), or add an equivalent fast privilege+table-lock recheck for the PointGet short-path before returning a cached plan/executor. Keep the “no MatchOpts” optimization separate from privilege enforcement.
entries.verify: Add a regression test: user A prepares a PK PointGet statement (to enable point short path), executes it enough times to populate `stmt.PointGet.Executor` and get a plan-cache hit, then user/root revokes SELECT on the table; next EXECUTE must error. Also add a variant under `LOCK TABLES` / table-lock scenario to ensure lock checks still apply on cache hits.
entries.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:222` sets `isPointPlan=true` when `stmt.PointGet.Executor != nil` and does `Get(cacheKey, nil)`; `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:247` skips `checkPreparedPriv` when `isPointPlan` is true; `pkg/planner/optimize.go:510` `OptimizeExecStmt` does not perform privilege/table-lock checks and relies on plan-cache path; `pkg/session/session.go:2142` executes point plan short path (`stmt.PointGet`) when `stmt.PsStmt != nil`, with no additional privilege enforcement.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed later: upstream `master` at `b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943` still derives `skipPrivCheck` from `stmt.PointGet.Executor != nil` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:227` in upstream/master view) and conditionally skips `checkPreparedPriv` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:304` in upstream/master view).

entries.subject: expression: JSON_SCHEMA_VALID() (#52780)
entries.what: `JSON_SCHEMA_VALID()` introduces a dependency (`github.com/qri-io/jsonschema`) whose default behavior can perform external schema resolution via `$ref` (HTTP/file) and uses a package-global mutable registry implemented with unguarded maps. When invoked from SQL, this enables SSRF/local file access attempts and creates a realistic risk of TiDB panics/data races under concurrent use; the function also uses `context.Background()` so any external fetch cannot be canceled/timed out.
entries.impact:
Security + stability risk:
- SSRF: a user can craft a schema with `$ref` pointing to arbitrary `http/https` URLs; TiDB will issue outbound requests during `JSON_SCHEMA_VALID` evaluation.
- Local file read attempts: schema `$ref` with `file://...` triggers server-side file reads (at least existence/parse side channels; may be extended depending on schema behavior).
- DoS: remote fetch has no timeout/cancel and leaks `res.Body` (FD/resource leak), so queries can hang and/or exhaust resources.
- Concurrency crash/data race: the dependency uses a package-global registry with unprotected Go maps; concurrent validations involving `$id` registration or `$ref` fetching can lead to `concurrent map read and map write` panics.
- Cross-session nondeterminism/state pollution: global registry entries can be overwritten by user input, affecting other sessions’ `$ref` resolution.
This commit also adds `ast.JSONSchemaValid` into `GAFunction4ExpressionIndex` (`pkg/sessionctx/variable/varsutil.go`), expanding the number of places this behavior can be triggered (generated/expression index evaluation, DDL/index build, etc.).
entries.fix:
Do not allow external I/O or global mutable state during SQL expression evaluation.
- Prefer switching to a JSON-schema validator that does not do network/file fetching and does not use global registries.
- If staying on this dependency, fork/patch it (or wrap it) to: (1) disable `FetchSchema` / remote `$ref` resolution (only allow local-fragment refs), (2) remove the package-global registry or make it per-validation and concurrency-safe, and (3) close HTTP response bodies + enforce timeouts.
- In TiDB, additionally pre-scan the input schema JSON and reject/raise error when encountering `$ref` with absolute URI/schemes (`http:`, `https:`, `file:`) and potentially `$id` that would register into a shared registry.
- Pass a cancellable context derived from statement execution (not `context.Background()`) if any potentially-blocking work remains.
entries.verify:
- Add an integration/unit test where schema contains `$ref: "http://127.0.0.1:PORT/schema"` and assert TiDB rejects it without attempting network I/O.
- Add a test that validates schemas with `$id` under concurrent goroutines/sessions to ensure no panic and no shared global mutation.
- Add regression coverage that execution respects statement cancellation/timeouts if any blocking work remains.
- Security review: explicitly document and assert that JSON_SCHEMA_VALID is pure/deterministic and performs no external I/O.
entries.evidence:
TiDB wires the builtin to `github.com/qri-io/jsonschema` and validates via `schema.ValidateBytes(context.Background(), ...)` (no statement cancellation / timeout): `pkg/expression/builtin_json.go:1846`-`pkg/expression/builtin_json.go:1893`.

Dependency behavior (github.com/qri-io/jsonschema v0.2.1, as introduced by this commit in `go.mod`):
- `$ref` can resolve/fetch external schemas: `GetSchemaRegistry().Get(ctx, address)` in `/Users/bba/.gvm/pkgsets/go1.25.1/global/pkg/mod/github.com/qri-io/jsonschema@v0.2.1/keywords_core.go:257`-`.../keywords_core.go:310`.
- Global registry is a package-level singleton `var sr *SchemaRegistry` with unguarded maps and writes (race/panic risk): `/Users/bba/.gvm/pkgsets/go1.25.1/global/pkg/mod/github.com/qri-io/jsonschema@v0.2.1/schema_registry.go:9`-`.../schema_registry.go:26`, `.../schema_registry.go:34`-`.../schema_registry.go:52`, `.../schema_registry.go:68`-`.../schema_registry.go:74`.
- Remote fetch supports `http/https` and `file` schemes and uses `http.Client{}` (no timeout) and does not close `res.Body`: `/Users/bba/.gvm/pkgsets/go1.25.1/global/pkg/mod/github.com/qri-io/jsonschema@v0.2.1/util.go:55`-`.../util.go:93`.
- `$id` registration can write into the global registry during validation: `/Users/bba/.gvm/pkgsets/go1.25.1/global/pkg/mod/github.com/qri-io/jsonschema@v0.2.1/schema.go:71`-`.../schema.go:84`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `pkg/expression/builtin_json.go` still calls `schema.ValidateBytes(context.Background(), ...)` and `go.mod` still depends on `github.com/qri-io/jsonschema v0.2.1`, so the external-I/O/global-registry risks remain.

entries.subject: planner: use code-gen to generate CloneForPlanCache method for Insert/Update/Delete (#55185)
entries.what: `(*expression.Assignment).Clone()` can panic when cloning lazy-error `ON DUPLICATE` assignments because it unconditionally calls `a.Expr.Clone()` even though `Expr` is allowed to be nil when `LazyErr` is set (deferred `ErrSubqueryMoreThan1Row` path). This breaks `Insert.CloneForPlanCache` (and any other use of `util.CloneAssignments`) under instance plan cache.
entries.impact: With instance plan cache enabled, cloning a cached `Insert` plan containing `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` assignments that carry `LazyErr` (e.g. deferred `ErrSubqueryMoreThan1Row`) can panic during `CloneForPlanCache`, turning an expected conditional runtime error into a panic/failure before duplicate detection. This can break cross-session plan reuse and can surface as a server-side panic in the plan-cache clone path.
entries.fix:
Make `(*expression.Assignment).Clone()` nil-safe for `Expr` (and ideally `Col`) so lazy-error assignments clone without panicking, e.g.:
- If `a == nil` return nil.
- If `a.Col != nil` clone it, else keep nil.
- If `a.Expr != nil` clone it, else keep nil.
Optionally also harden `util.CloneAssignments` to tolerate nil elements.
entries.verify:
Add a regression test that:
- Enables instance plan cache and `EnablePlanCacheForSubquery`.
- Prepares an `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = (SELECT ...)` where the scalar subquery can trigger `ErrSubqueryMoreThan1Row` during preprocessing.
- Executes in session 1 to populate the instance cache, then executes in session 2 to force `CloneForPlanCache`.
Expect: no panic during clone; statement only errors when the duplicate-update path is actually taken.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/expression/expression.go:815` adds `(*Assignment).Clone()` and unconditionally calls `a.Expr.Clone()` (`pkg/expression/expression.go:819`).
`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3838` builds `Insert.OnDuplicate` assignments with `Expr: expr` and `LazyErr: err`; for the special-cased `ErrSubqueryMoreThan1Row`, it keeps `err` and continues (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3840`), meaning `expr` can be nil.
`rewriteExprNode()` returns `(nil, nil, err)` when the rewriter hits an error (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:304-306`). One concrete producer is scalar-subquery preprocessing: it executes `EvalSubqueryFirstRow(...)` and propagates its error (incl. `ErrSubqueryMoreThan1Row`) (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1346-1349`).
Plan-cache cloning hits this path: `Insert.CloneForPlanCache` clones `OnDuplicate` via `util.CloneAssignments` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_clone_generated.go:462-468`), which calls `a.Clone()` for each assignment (`pkg/planner/util/misc.go:96-105`). If `a.Expr == nil`, this panics.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream-master` (`6d5529545b451c376b2e9bba31620bab34430fa7`): `upstream-master:pkg/expression/expression.go` still has `Expr: a.Expr.Clone()` without a nil guard, and `upstream-master` still documents that `asgn.Expr` can be nil when `LazyErr` exists (moved file: `upstream-master:pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/physical_common_plans.go`).

entries.subject: planner: Removed check for prepared stmt during partition pruning (#55631)
entries.what: Prepared plan-cache correctness regression: removing the plan-cache-aware const check allows `PartitionPruning` to evaluate parameter markers during prepared-plan building, so global index scans can get a constant `_tidb_pid IN (...)` partition filter derived from the *first* execution’s parameter values and then cache that plan, yielding wrong results for later executions with different parameter values.
entries.impact: Prepared statement plan-cache can return wrong results (missing rows) on cache hit when partition-pruning conditions (e.g. `a = ?`) steer the baked `_tidb_pid IN (...)` list to different partitions across executions. This is a silent correctness/data-visibility bug.
entries.fix:
Do not bake parameter-value-dependent partition IDs into a cacheable plan. Options:
- If `StmtCtx.InPreparedPlanBuilding` is true (plan generation for caching) and pruning depends on non-`ConstStrict` constants (e.g. param markers / deferred expr), skip adding the `_tidb_pid IN (...)` filter (treat as FullRange) OR call `StmtCtx.SetSkipPlanCache(...)` when such a filter would be added.
- Alternatively, rebuild the global-index `_tidb_pid` filter per execution on cache hit (similar to `rebuildRange`), but that is a larger change.
- Keep executor-time partition pruning for prepared statements by distinguishing plan-build vs execution (e.g. key off `InPreparedPlanBuilding`, not `UseCache`).
entries.verify:
Add a regression test:
- Create a range-partitioned table with multiple partitions and a global index plan path.
- `prepare stmt from 'select /*+ use_index(t, idx) */ ... where part_col = ? and idx_col = ?'`.
- Execute with params hitting partition P1; confirm result and `@@last_plan_from_cache` behavior.
- Execute with params hitting partition P2; ensure cache hit still returns correct rows (no stale `_tidb_pid` list).
entries.evidence:
In `pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go`, `rangePruner.extractDataForPrune` no longer gates on `expression.ConstExprConsiderPlanCache(constExpr, sctx.GetSessionVars().StmtCtx.UseCache())` and now directly evaluates `constExpr.EvalInt(..., chunk.Row{})`.

Planner uses `PartitionPruning` results to bake a constant partition-id filter for global index scans: `pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go` `(*PhysicalIndexScan).addSelectionConditionForGlobalIndex` calls `PartitionPruning(...)` and then appends `expression.NewInt64Const(pInfo.Definitions[idx].ID)` into an `IN(t._tidb_pid, ...)` predicate.

Prepared plan-cache flow: `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go` caches the optimized physical plan when `stmtCtx.UseCache()` remains true; `pkg/planner/core/plan_cacheable_checker.go` allows partitioned tables when dynamic prune is enabled; `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_rebuild.go` only rebuilds ranges, not this `_tidb_pid` constant list. So a param-dependent pid list becomes fixed in the cached plan.

Second confirmation: Param markers are represented as `*expression.Constant` with `ParamMarker != nil`, so `ConstLevel()==ConstOnlyInContext` (`pkg/expression/constant.go`). Previously, `ConstExprConsiderPlanCache(..., inPlanCache=true)` would return false (`pkg/expression/util.go`), preventing pruning in plan-cache building and avoiding baking param-dependent partition IDs.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: the same pattern still exists (moved code uses `partitionpruning.PartitionPruning` and still builds constant `_tidb_pid IN (const ...)` filters, with no plan-cache safety gate), so it does not appear fixed later.

entries.subject: planner: Removed check for prepared stmt during partition pruning (#55631)
entries.what: Crash regression risk: removing the const-expression guard means `extractDataForPrune` can attempt to `EvalInt` an expression that still contains column references using `chunk.Row{}` (nil chunk), which can panic.
entries.impact: Server panic (nil pointer dereference) during partition pruning for valid partition expressions where column references remain after `replaceColumnWithConst` (e.g. `PARTITION BY RANGE (a + a)` and query predicate `a = 2`). This is a hard crash and can be triggered by user SQL.
entries.fix:
Reintroduce a safety gate before `EvalInt` that only rejects truly non-constant expressions, while still allowing param markers:
- Minimal: `if constExpr.ConstLevel() == expression.ConstNone { return ret, false }`.
- Or implement a full-column replacement (replace all occurrences of the partition column in `partFn`) before evaluation.
Either prevents evaluating expressions that still reference columns with an empty `chunk.Row{}`.
entries.verify: Add a regression test that creates a partitioned table with an expression like `a + a` (or any expression where the partition column appears more than once) and runs `SELECT ... WHERE a = <const>` (and `a IN (...)`) under static/dynamic prune modes; it should not panic and should return correct results (pruning may conservatively fall back).
entries.evidence:
In this commit, `pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go` `rangePruner.extractDataForPrune` now unconditionally executes `constExpr.EvalInt(..., chunk.Row{})` after `replaceColumnWithConst(p.partFn, con)`.

`replaceColumnWithConst` only replaces a single argument position (`args[0]=con`, or a couple of special cases) and does not rewrite all column occurrences. `makePartitionByFnCol` only checks `expression.ExtractColumnSet(args...).Len()==1`, which can be true even if the same column appears multiple times (e.g. partition expression `a + a`), so `constExpr` can still contain an `*expression.Column` after replacement.

Evaluating an expression containing a column with `chunk.Row{}` panics: `pkg/expression/column.go` `(*Column).EvalInt` calls `row.IsNull` / `row.GetDatum`; `pkg/util/chunk/row.go` implements these via `r.c.columns[...]` and `chunk.Row{}` has `c==nil`.

Second confirmation: Previously, the removed `ConstExprConsiderPlanCache` gate would have rejected such non-constant expressions because `Column.ConstLevel()==ConstNone` (`pkg/expression/column.go`) and `ScalarFunction.ConstLevel()` returns `ConstNone` if any arg is `ConstNone` (`pkg/expression/scalar_function.go`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: partition pruning still evaluates `constExpr.EvalInt(..., chunk.Row{})` without restoring a `ConstNone` guard, and `Column.EvalInt` still assumes a non-empty row, so this panic risk appears unfixed later.

entries.subject: executor: ignore foreign key error in `UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE ignore` (#56682)
entries.what: Referred-FK (parent-side) UPDATE/ON-DUP-UPDATE is checked against the wrong row image in IGNORE mode, so 1451 violations can be missed and applied (no warning), breaking FK integrity.
entries.impact: Data consistency / SQL semantics: `UPDATE IGNORE` and `INSERT IGNORE ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` can silently apply parent key changes that should be rejected (1451) under RESTRICT/NO ACTION, potentially leaving orphan child rows and breaking foreign key invariants; also diverges from expected IGNORE behavior (should skip offending row and emit warning).
entries.fix: When `IGNORE` is in effect, FK pre-check must distinguish FK types: for `FK != nil` (modify child), check `newRow`; for `ReferredFK != nil` (modify parent with RESTRICT/NO ACTION), check `oldRow` (the key currently referenced by children). Concretely, avoid calling `checkFKIgnoreErr` once on a single row for all `fkChecks`; instead run per-check with the correct row source (or change `checkFKIgnoreErr` to accept both `oldRow/newRow` and branch internally). Also avoid skipping the normal FK trigger pipeline for successful rows unless equivalent locking/checking is preserved.
entries.verify: Add/extend assertions for the existing integration cases: `tests/integrationtest/t/executor/update.test:697` and `tests/integrationtest/t/executor/insert.test:1610`. Verify that parent-side 1451 under IGNORE emits a warning and does not change the parent key (e.g., `select` after the IGNORE statement shows parent row unchanged and child still references an existing parent), and that child-side 1452 still becomes warning + skipped row. Minimal SQL repro: create parent/child with FK on `ref`, make a child reference `ref=2`, then run `update ignore parent set ref=3 where id=2` / `insert ignore into parent values (2,3) on duplicate key update ref=3` and ensure it warns 1451 and leaves `parent.ref` as 2.
entries.evidence: UPDATE IGNORE pre-check always checks `newTableData`: `pkg/executor/update.go:212`, then calls `updateRecord(..., ignoreErr=true)`: `pkg/executor/update.go:222`. INSERT IGNORE ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE does the same with `newData`: `pkg/executor/insert.go:482` and `pkg/executor/insert.go:492`. But FK semantics for referred-FK (parent being updated) must check the *old* referenced key: `FKCheckExec.updateRowNeedToCheck` uses `oldRow` when `fkc.ReferredFK != nil`: `pkg/executor/foreign_key.go:168` and `pkg/executor/foreign_key.go:195`. Because `updateRecord` skips `updateRowNeedToCheck` entirely when `ignoreErr=true`: `pkg/executor/write.go:224`, referred-FK violations (1451) can be missed and the update applied. Integration outputs added/updated in this commit show no warning emitted for the parent-side 1451 cases (file ends immediately after the IGNORE statement): `tests/integrationtest/r/executor/update.result:905` and `tests/integrationtest/r/executor/insert.result:2144`. Checked later history: still not fixed on `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`), same missing warning lines at `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/update.result:905` and `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/insert.result:2147`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed as of `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): unchanged behavior in integration outputs (`upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/update.result:905`, `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/insert.result:2147`) and ignore-FK precheck remains `newData`-based (see `upstream/master:pkg/executor/write.go:250`).

entries.subject: planner: optimize the performance of PointPlan for Instance Plan Cache (#57260)
entries.what: `FastClonePointGetForPlanCache` clears `Handle` and does not copy `IndexValues`, but rebuild only restores parameter-driven slots; point-get plans with any literal key component can lose required key values on instance plan cache hits, causing panics or wrong results.
entries.impact: With `tidb_enable_instance_plan_cache=1`, repeated executions (after `stmt.PointGet.Executor` becomes non-nil) of prepared point-get statements containing literal constants can crash (table point get: `Handle` remains nil) or return incorrect results (unique key point get: constant `IndexValues` slots remain unset). This is a correctness + availability risk in a hot path (point get + plan cache).
entries.fix:
In `FastClonePointGetForPlanCache`, preserve immutable key parts:
- If `src.HandleConstant == nil`, copy `src.Handle` into `dst.Handle` (e.g. `dst.Handle = src.Handle.Copy()`) instead of forcing nil.
- Initialize `dst.IndexValues` from `src.IndexValues` for slots where `src.IndexConstants[i] == nil` (or simply copy/clone the whole `IndexValues` slice, then let rebuild overwrite param slots).
Add regression cases under instance plan cache for point-get with literals (e.g. `pk=1`, and mixed `a=? AND b=1`).
entries.verify:
Repro in a single session with instance plan cache enabled (needs 2nd execution to hit cache + executor reuse):
1) `set global tidb_enable_instance_plan_cache=1;`
2) `create table t(a int primary key, b int, unique key uk(a,b)); insert into t values(1,1);`
3) Case A (literal handle): `prepare s from 'select * from t where a=1'; execute s; execute s;` (2nd exec may panic or misbehave).
4) Case B (mixed literal/index): `prepare s2 from 'select * from t where a=? and b=1'; set @a=1; execute s2 using @a; execute s2 using @a;` (2nd exec may return empty/wrong).
Confirm it only occurs when instance plan cache is enabled and after executor reuse (`stmt.PointGet.Executor` becomes non-nil).
entries.evidence:
`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:229` calls `clonePlanForInstancePlanCache` on instance-plan-cache hits; when `stmt.PointGet.Executor != nil` and plan is `*PointGetPlan`, it uses `FastClonePointGetForPlanCache` into `stmt.PointGet.FastPlan` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache.go:242`).
`FastClonePointGetForPlanCache` unconditionally clears key fields instead of preserving constants: `dst.Handle = nil` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_clone_utils.go:191`) and only resizes `dst.IndexValues` without copying from `src` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_clone_utils.go:203`).
Rebuild does not restore literal constants: `buildRangesForPointGet` sets `Handle` only when `HandleConstant != nil` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_rebuild.go:295`) and sets `IndexValues[i]` only when `IndexConstants[i] != nil` (`pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_rebuild.go:307`). But literals produce `con == nil` in `getNameValuePairs` (`pkg/planner/core/point_get_plan.go:1676`), so fast-path `PointGetPlan.HandleConstant`/`IndexConstants[i]` can be nil for literals (`pkg/planner/core/point_get_plan.go:1367`, `pkg/planner/core/point_get_plan.go:1438`).
Runtime relies on these values: `PointGetExecutor` encodes the row key with `e.handle` without nil checks (`pkg/executor/point_get.go:387`), and unique-index point get encodes keys from `e.idxVals` (`pkg/executor/point_get.go:308`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master`: `pkg/planner/core/plan_clone_utils.go:25` still sets `dst.Handle = nil` and does not copy `IndexValues` before rebuild; `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_rebuild.go:256` still only fills `Handle`/`IndexValues` from non-nil `HandleConstant`/`IndexConstants`.

entries.subject: planner: provide a system view information_schema.tidb_plan_cache to allow users to see info in the cache (#57699)
entries.what: `information_schema.tidb_plan_cache` exposes cached SQL text and parameter values for all users without privilege/visibility controls (no `PROCESS` gating or per-user filtering), enabling cross-user information disclosure.
entries.impact: Privilege/visibility violation: any user who can query `information_schema.tidb_plan_cache` can read other users’ cached SQL text, bindings, and compile-time parameter values (potential secrets/PII) from the instance plan cache. This can leak metadata and sensitive values across users/tenants.
entries.fix:
Gate `information_schema.tidb_plan_cache` behind `PROCESS` (or a suitable dynamic privilege like `RESTRICTED_TABLES_ADMIN`), or filter rows to current `user@host` unless `PROCESS` is granted.
Consider redacting or omitting `PARSE_VALUES`/`SQL_TEXT` for non-privileged users (and under SEM), aligning with existing visibility rules for statement text in `processlist`-like tables.
entries.verify:
1) Create two users `u1`, `u2` with minimal privileges.
2) As `u1`, execute a prepared statement containing a sensitive parameter so it enters instance plan cache.
3) As `u2` (without `PROCESS`), run `SELECT SQL_TEXT, PARSE_VALUES, PARSE_USER FROM information_schema.tidb_plan_cache`.
Expected after fix: access denied (requires `PROCESS`/dynamic privilege) or only `u2`’s own entries are visible; no cross-user SQL/param leakage.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/executor/infoschema_reader.go:3907` exposes all entries from `domain.GetDomain(sctx).GetInstancePlanCache().All()` and returns `SQLText` / `ParseUser` / `ParseValues` etc with no `PROCESS` privilege check or per-user filtering.
`pkg/infoschema/tables.go:1725` defines sensitive columns `SQL_TEXT` and `PARSE_VALUES` (LONG_BLOB).
Contrast: `information_schema.processlist` is filtered by `PROCESS` privilege / login user in `pkg/executor/infoschema_reader.go:1784`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed as of `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `upstream/master:pkg/executor/infoschema_reader.go` still builds plan-cache rows without any `PROCESS` privilege gating/filtering while returning `SQLText` and `ParseValues`.

entries.subject: executor: run idxlookup workers in a pool (#58033)
entries.what: Deadlock risk when index lookup concurrency is 1: the index scan runs as a task in the same worker pool whose `MaxWorkers` is also 1, so table lookup tasks can’t run until the index scan finishes. If the index scan produces more than the `resultCh` buffer (default 50) it blocks on `resultCh` while `Next()` is blocked on `task.doneCh`, causing an indefinite hang.
entries.impact: If `tidb_index_lookup_concurrency`/`tidb_executor_concurrency` is 1 and the index scan produces more than `LookupTableTaskChannelSize` lookup tasks (e.g. large scans where tasks > 50), the index task can block on `resultCh` while all table tasks are queued but cannot run (no available pool worker). The session goroutine is simultaneously blocked on `task.doneCh`, causing the query to hang indefinitely.
entries.fix:
Ensure table lookups can run concurrently with the index scan even when `e.indexLookupConcurrency == 1`:
- Prefer: keep index worker as a dedicated goroutine (outside the pool) and use the pool only for table tasks (so `MaxWorkers` maps 1:1 to table concurrency, as before).
- Alternative: set pool capacity to include the index task (e.g. `MaxWorkers = e.indexLookupConcurrency + 1`) and spawn a worker as soon as there is any pending table task (don’t require `tasks > 1` / `TolerablePendingTasks=1` when the only running worker is the index task).
entries.verify:
Minimal repro (manual): set `tidb_executor_concurrency=1` (or `tidb_index_lookup_concurrency=1`), run a query that uses IndexLookupExecutor and returns > ~1,000,000 handles (so >50 batches at 20k/batch) and confirm it can complete.
Stronger (unit/integration): temporarily set `executor.LookupTableTaskChannelSize=1` (as done in `pkg/executor/test/seqtest/seq_executor_test.go`) with concurrency=1 and ensure the query does not hang.
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/distsql.go:641-653` builds a `workerPool` with `MaxWorkers = max(1, e.indexLookupConcurrency)` and no extra slot for the index task; the index scan itself is executed in that same pool via `e.pool.submit(...)` (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:732-814`). Each lookup task enqueues a table task into the pool and then immediately sends the task to `resultCh` (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:1085-1097`), while the consumer blocks on `<-task.doneCh` before it can advance (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:956-965`). `resultCh` is buffered by `LookupTableTaskChannelSize` (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:619`), which defaults to 50 (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:74-75`). Concurrency can be set to 1 (`pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:2072-2074`). With `MaxWorkers=1`, the pool cannot spawn a second worker (`pkg/executor/utils.go:134-165`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): the same pattern remains (index task runs in the same pool capped by `indexLookupConcurrency`, and table tasks are pool tasks).

entries.subject: planner: remove redundant branches in the OR list (#58962)
entries.what: `removeRedundantORBranch` removes “duplicates” in OR lists using `string(expr.HashCode())` as the sole identity key. `HashCode()` is not a full identity for expressions with differing `RetType` (notably `CAST`, and also constants/collation), so this can incorrectly drop non-equivalent OR branches and change SQL semantics.
entries.impact: Potential wrong-results: semantically different predicates can be dropped if they collide on `HashCode()`. A concrete class is predicates differing only by `CAST` target `RetType` flags/collation (e.g., `CAST(a AS SIGNED)` vs `CAST(a AS UNSIGNED)`), which can change boolean outcomes yet share the same `HashCode()` today.
entries.fix: Don’t treat `HashCode()` equality as definitive equality. Keep a representative expression per key and confirm with `Equals` (or store a slice and check any `Equals`) before dropping an item. Alternatively, key by `Hash64` and still resolve collisions with `Equals` (since `Hash64` includes `RetType`).
entries.verify: Add a planner test that exercises an OR list with two branches that differ only in `CAST` target flags/collation and produce different results, then ensure both branches remain after predicate simplification (via `EXPLAIN` operator info) and/or that query results match MySQL. Example pattern: `... WHERE (CAST(a AS SIGNED) < 0) OR (CAST(a AS UNSIGNED) < 0)` with `a` a signed integer column containing negative values; the two branches are not redundant and must not be deduped.
entries.evidence:
Planner dedups OR items solely by `HashCode()` bytes: `pkg/planner/core/rule_predicate_simplification.go:428`-`pkg/planner/core/rule_predicate_simplification.go:471` (key line: `pkg/planner/core/rule_predicate_simplification.go:458`).
But `HashCode()` is lossy vs expression equality w.r.t. `RetType` (esp. `CAST`): `pkg/expression/scalar_function.go:700`-`pkg/expression/scalar_function.go:724` compares `RetType` while `ReHashCode` only appends `EvalType` for cast: `pkg/expression/scalar_function.go:726`-`pkg/expression/scalar_function.go:739`.
`CAST` semantics do depend on target flags like unsigned: `pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:874`-`pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:891`, and comparisons use unsigned flags from `GetType().GetFlag()`: `pkg/expression/builtin_compare.go:3040`-`pkg/expression/builtin_compare.go:3052`.
Upstream/master still has the same `HashCode()`-only dedup: `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_predicate_simplification.go:509`-`upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_predicate_simplification.go:544`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed later: `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_predicate_simplification.go:509`-`upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_predicate_simplification.go:544` still uses `hashCode := string(orItem.HashCode())` with no `Equals` check.

entries.subject: privilege/privileges:  refactor the data struct for user privilege data (#58945)
entries.what: `Handle.UpdateAll()` stores a fully-loaded privilege cache without initializing `globalVars` and without enforcing deterministic per-user ordering for tables that use first-match resolution (`global_priv`, `tables_priv`, `columns_priv`), so privilege/auth matching can select the wrong host-pattern row after `UpdateAll()`.
entries.impact: After `Handle.UpdateAll()` (reachable via `NotifyUpdateAllUsersPrivilege`/`FLUSH PRIVILEGES`, and also via `UpdateAllActive()` fallback when `activeUsers` > 1024), privilege/auth decisions can become dependent on storage scan order: `matchTables`/`matchColumns`/`matchGlobalPriv` return the first match, so a less-specific host pattern (e.g. `'%') may be chosen before a more-specific one (e.g. `'localhost'`), potentially granting/denying table/column privileges incorrectly and potentially bypassing or misapplying SSL/login restrictions stored in `mysql.global_priv`. Additionally, missing `globalVars` wiring in `UpdateAll()` can mis-assign `AuthPlugin` when `mysql.user.plugin` is empty (default auth plugin should come from `@@global.default_authentication_plugin`).
entries.fix: In `Handle.UpdateAll()`, set `priv.globalVars = h.globalVars` before `priv.LoadAll(...)`. Ensure `LoadAll()` results are ordered for first-match lookups by sorting per-user slices after load (e.g. in each `Load*Table` add `p.<tree>.Ascend(func(itm ...) { slices.SortFunc(itm.data, compareX); return true })` for `globalPriv`, `tablesPriv`, `columnsPriv` (and `db` too), or add a dedicated `p.sortAll()` called at end of `LoadAll()`).
entries.verify: Add a regression covering the `UpdateAll()` path (not just merge path): create both `user@'%'` and `user@'localhost'` entries with conflicting `mysql.tables_priv`/`mysql.columns_priv` (and `mysql.global_priv` SSL flags), call `Handle.UpdateAll()` then assert `RequestVerification()` and `ConnectionVerification()` pick the most-specific host row. Also cover the `UpdateAllActive()` fallback by simulating `activeUsers` > 1024 and confirming privilege results remain deterministic.
entries.evidence: `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:2070` `Handle.UpdateAll()` creates `priv := newMySQLPrivilege()` then calls `priv.LoadAll(h.sctx)` and `h.priv.Store(priv)` but does not set `priv.globalVars` and does not sort per-user record slices after load. `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:435` `MySQLPrivilege.LoadAll()` calls `LoadGlobalPrivTable/LoadTablesPrivTable/LoadColumnsPrivTable`. Those load methods (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:816`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:864`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:873`) only append decoded rows and do not sort. Lookups are first-match: `matchGlobalPriv`/`matchTables`/`matchColumns` return the first matching record in `item.data` (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1378`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1421`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1435`). Sorting is explicitly relied upon elsewhere: merge sorts `itm.data` for these tables (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:612`..`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:666`). `pkg/domain/domain.go:2944` shows `NotifyUpdatePrivilege` calls `do.PrivilegeHandle().UpdateAll()` when `event.All` (e.g. `FLUSH PRIVILEGES`), and `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:2089` shows `UpdateAllActive()` can fall back to `UpdateAll()` when active users > 1024.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `pingcap/master` (at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `Handle.UpdateAll()` still loads via `LoadAll()` and stores directly; `LoadTablesPrivTable`/`LoadColumnsPrivTable`/`LoadGlobalPrivTable` still do not sort per-user slices, and `matchTables` remains first-match, so this ordering hazard is not fully removed upstream.

entries.subject: table: use writable columns to avoid columns not match when add column DDL exec parallel with update DML (#60048)
entries.what: Potential panic regression for partitioned tables: switching `partitionedTable`’s eval buffer from `Cols()` to `WritableCols()` makes the in-memory row layout incompatible with INSERT rows that include `_tidb_rowid` during ADD COLUMN `StateWriteOnly`. The `_tidb_rowid` datum can be written into the new write-only column slot during `locatePartition`, and for some types this triggers a runtime panic in `chunk.MutRow.SetDatum` due to too-short backing buffers.
entries.impact: TiDB can panic/crash while locating the target partition for an INSERT that explicitly sets `_tidb_rowid` during ADD COLUMN `StateWriteOnly` on a partitioned table without clustered PK. This is a correctness/availability issue (process crash) and can be triggered by common new-column types with small/empty initial buffers (e.g. `FLOAT`, `VARCHAR`, `JSON`).
entries.fix: In `pkg/table/tables/partition.go:1745` (`partitionedTableAddRecord`), detect insert rows that include `_tidb_rowid` (e.g. `len(r) > len(t.Cols())` and `!opt.IsUpdate()`), and pass a sanitized row to `locatePartition` that excludes the extra-handle datum and (optionally) extends to `len(t.WritableCols())` with NULL/default placeholders for write-only columns. Alternative robust fix: in `locateRangeColumnPartition`/`locateRangePartition`/`locateHashPartition`, avoid `SetDatums(r...)` and instead set only the referenced partition-column offsets, leaving all other slots NULL.
entries.verify:
Add a regression test similar to `pkg/ddl/db_table_test.go`’s `_tidb_rowid` + add-column-in-write-only scenario, but on a partitioned table:
1) Create partitioned table without clustered PK (so `_tidb_rowid` exists) and enable `set @@tidb_opt_write_row_id=1`.
2) Use the `beforeRunOneJobStep` hook at `job.SchemaState == model.StateWriteOnly` to run `insert into t(...,_tidb_rowid) values (...)`.
3) Concurrently run `alter table t add column d varchar(10) not null default ''` (or `float`).
Expected: no panic and insert succeeds. Current code can panic in `pkg/util/chunk/mutrow.go:SetDatum` during partition locating.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/table/tables/partition.go:368` builds `evalBufferTypes` from `t.WritableCols()` and appends an extra-handle type at the end when `!PKIsHandle`; `pkg/table/tables/partition.go:1498`/`1548`/`1603` call `evalBuffer.SetDatums(r...)`.
For INSERT, the row passed to `partitionedTableAddRecord` is shaped as “public cols (+ optional `_tidb_rowid`)”: `pkg/executor/insert_common.go:336` sizes `rowLen := len(e.Table.Cols())` and `+1` when `_tidb_rowid` is present; `_tidb_rowid` is assigned offset `len(cols)` by `pkg/table/column.go:164`.
When an ADD COLUMN is in `StateWriteOnly`, the new column is included in `WritableCols()` but not `Cols()`, so `_tidb_rowid`’s offset collides with the new write-only column slot in the eval buffer. `chunk.MutRow.SetDatum` writes int64 datums via `binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(col.data, ...)` (`pkg/util/chunk/mutrow.go:306`), which panics if that column’s backing buffer is <8 bytes; `MutRowFromTypes` initializes VARCHAR/VARSTRING columns with `""` (`pkg/util/chunk/mutrow.go:94`), resulting in a 0-length `col.data` for that slot.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream-master` (`6d5529545b45`): `initEvalBufferType` still uses `WritableCols()` and the locate code still calls `evalBuffer.SetDatums(r...)` unchanged, so no later fix was found in `pkg/table/tables/partition.go`.

entries.subject: planner: Handle NullEQ <=> in range columns partition pruning (#61187)
entries.what: Partition pruning can panic on `const <=> col` (NullEQ) because operand-swapping calls `opposite()` with `ast.NullEQ`, but `opposite()` doesn’t handle `ast.NullEQ`.
entries.impact: A user can trigger a planner panic (potential server crash/DoS or at least statement failure, depending on panic recovery) with queries that put the constant on the left of `<=>` against a RANGE / RANGE COLUMNS partitioning column, e.g. `SELECT ... FROM t WHERE 'D' <=> a` or `NULL <=> a`. This is a correctness/availability regression introduced by accepting `ast.NullEQ` without updating `opposite()`.
entries.fix: Treat `ast.NullEQ` as symmetric in the swap logic: either add `case ast.NullEQ: return ast.NullEQ` to `opposite()`, or special-case callers to skip `opposite()` when `op==ast.NullEQ` (both in RANGE and RANGE COLUMNS pruners).
entries.verify: Add planner tests that exercise constant-left `<=>` forms on partitioned tables, e.g. `explain ... where 'D' <=> a` and `explain ... where NULL <=> a`, for both `PARTITION BY RANGE` and `PARTITION BY RANGE COLUMNS`. Verify no panic and that pruning matches the existing constant-right behavior.
entries.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:1564` adds `ast.NullEQ` to the prunable operators. When the predicate is written as `const <=> col`, `extractDataForPrune` swaps operands via `ret.op = opposite(ret.op)` (`pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:1583-1587`, also `:1594-1599` for CAST). But `opposite()` (`pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:1708-1721`) has no `ast.NullEQ` case and panics on unknown ops. Same pattern exists in RANGE COLUMNS pruning: `rangeColumnsPruner.partitionRangeForExpr` calls `opName = opposite(opName)` when the column is on the right (`pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:2063-2067`, also `:2074-2079`). Second confirmation (different evidence): expression rewriting preserves operand order (no canonical swap) when building `NullEQ`: `binaryOpToExpression` calls `constructBinaryOpFunction(lhs, rhs, op)` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1787-1794`), and the base case emits `newFunction(op, ..., l, r)` unchanged (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:401-405`), so user SQL like `'D' <=> a` will indeed produce `nulleq(constant, column)` and hit the swap path.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_partition_processor.go` still allows `ast.NullEQ` and still executes `ret.Op = opposite(ret.Op)` on swapped args (`...:1604` in the upstream/master view), while `opposite()` still lacks a `ast.NullEQ` case and panics (`...:1681-1694` in the upstream/master view).

entries.subject: expression: deduplicate the args of IN function (#61249)
entries.what: `IN` integer-arg dedup can drop semantically distinct unsigned constants that collide in `int64` value with signed negatives (e.g. `18446744073709551615` vs `-1`), causing `IN`/`NOT IN` to return incorrect results (values explicitly present in the list can be treated as absent).
entries.impact: Wrong results for `IN`/`NOT IN` involving unsigned BIGINT values > `math.MaxInt64` when the list also contains the corresponding negative signed literals (common patterns like `(-1, 18446744073709551615)` or `(-2, 18446744073709551614)`). This can cause incorrect filtering (returning rows that should be excluded) and can affect correctness of queries and DML relying on these predicates.
entries.fix:
For `builtinInIntSig`, dedup needs to account for signedness (and/or full uint64 value), not just `int64 val`:
- Treat `(val, isUnsigned)` as the uniqueness key when pruning `b.args`, so `-1` (signed) and `18446744073709551615` (unsigned) are not collapsed.
- Change `hashSet` to represent both signed/unsigned presence for the same `val` (e.g. `map[int64]uint8` bitset, or two sets), and make the membership check use the appropriate bit(s).
entries.verify:
Add/restore a correctness case where the predicate must exclude the explicit unsigned constants even if the list also contains `-1/-2`:
- `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a NOT IN (-1, -2, 18446744073709551615)` must not return `18446744073709551615`.
- `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a NOT IN (-1, -2, 0, 4, 18446744073709551614)` must not return `18446744073709551614`.
Also verify both TiDB (root) evaluation and coprocessor/pushdown behavior if applicable.
entries.evidence:
1) `pkg/expression/builtin_other.go:238` deduplicates int const args by `val` only (`if _, exists := b.hashSet[val]; !exists { ... }`), but the map value only stores a single unsigned-flag bit (`pkg/expression/builtin_other.go:203`, `pkg/expression/builtin_other.go:239`). This drops later constants that collide in int64 representation (e.g. `-1` vs `18446744073709551615`, `-2` vs `18446744073709551614`).
2) Regression is visible in existing integration output: `tests/integrationtest/r/expression/issues.result:319` runs `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a NOT IN (-1, -2, 18446744073709551615);`, but the result includes `18446744073709551615` at `tests/integrationtest/r/expression/issues.result:329` (and similarly `18446744073709551614` for the third query at `tests/integrationtest/r/expression/issues.result:339`).
3) Second confirmation via first-parent code: prior to this commit, `e7b038b^:pkg/expression/builtin_other.go:225` overwrote `b.hashSet[val] = ...` (last-wins), so the unsigned constant at the end could still be represented; now it is skipped entirely when an earlier signed constant shares the same `val`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): later commits touching `pkg/expression/builtin_other.go` are unrelated (e.g. `eb12403896` slices.Clone refactor; `9f38fcae00` variadic call), and `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/expression/issues.result` still shows the same `NOT IN` outputs including the explicitly excluded unsigned values.

entries.subject: planner: support `explain [analyze] <plan_digest>` for `explain explore` (#61942)
entries.what: SQL injection / privilege bypass via new `EXPLAIN <plan_digest>` path: `planDigest` (from `stringLit`) is interpolated directly into internal SQL executed through a system session, allowing crafted digests to alter the internal statement-summary query.
entries.impact: A user-controlled string literal can break out of the quoted `plan_digest` predicate in an internal SQL statement executed through a system session, enabling SQL injection into a privileged internal query. This can allow unauthorized data exposure (e.g., reading sensitive system tables via injected `UNION SELECT`), and potentially DoS via expanded scans, even if the caller lacks privileges to query statement-summary tables directly.
entries.fix:
- Parameterize `planDigest` in `fetchRecordFromClusterStmtSummary` using `ExecuteInternal` placeholders (e.g. `... where plan_digest = %? ...` and pass `planDigest` as args, twice) instead of `fmt.Sprintf(...'%s'...)`.
- Consider additionally validating `planDigest` format (length/hex) before querying, and/or gating `EXPLAIN <plan_digest>` behind an appropriate privilege (e.g. `PROCESS`/`SUPER`) since it consults statement summary.
entries.verify:
- Negative test: run `EXPLAIN 'x'' OR 1=1 -- '`; vulnerable behavior would return/act on unrelated stmt-summary rows instead of treating the digest as a literal value.
- Regression: ensure `EXPLAIN [ANALYZE] '<valid_plan_digest>'` still works for real digests.
- Security: attempt injected `UNION SELECT` that fabricates `query_sample_text` and confirm it cannot affect internal query results after parameterization.
entries.evidence:
- Parser introduces `EXPLAIN <stringLit>` as a new entrypoint that sets `ExplainStmt.PlanDigest` (`pkg/parser/parser.y:5621`-`pkg/parser/parser.y:5627`).
- Planner executes a stmt-summary lookup whenever `explain.PlanDigest != ""` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5622`-`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5628`), via `getHintedStmtThroughPlanDigest()` which runs under `AdvancedSysSessionPool` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5589`-`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5613`).
- The stmt-summary lookup builds SQL by string interpolation with **no escaping/parameters**: `... where plan_digest = '%s' ...` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:846`-`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:848`).
- Internal execution does not auto-escape unless args are supplied: `ExecuteInternal(..., sql, args...)` uses `ParseWithParams`, which only calls `sqlescape.EscapeSQL` when `len(args) > 0` (`pkg/session/session.go:1554`-`pkg/session/session.go:1580`, `pkg/session/session.go:1650`-`pkg/session/session.go:1655`).
- Privilege manager allows all checks when user/host are empty (common for internal/system sessions): `if p.user == "" && p.host == "" { return true }` (`pkg/privilege/privileges/privileges.go:150`-`pkg/privilege/privileges/privileges.go:157`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on later history up to `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): `fetchRecordFromClusterStmtSummary` still uses `fmt.Sprintf(... plan_digest = '%s' ...)` in `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go`.

entries.subject: codec: should also return the value even with error because the error may be ignored in the future (#62175)
entries.what: `HashGroupKey` now returns non-nil `buf` on decimal/time encode error (to survive when the error is downgraded), but it still returns immediately on the *first* row error. Because `GetGroupKey` may downgrade truncation errors to warnings/ignored via `ErrCtx`, HashAgg can proceed with a partially-filled `groupKey` (rows after the first error remain empty/missing suffix), leading to incorrect grouping/deduplication for chunks with more than one row.
entries.impact: Silent wrong results risk when `EncodeDecimal`/`EncodeMySQLTime` errors are treated as warnings/ignored: `HashGroupKey` may return a partially-filled `groupKey` where rows after the first error keep empty/missing key bytes. HashAgg will then merge unrelated rows into the same group (or drop distinct values), corrupting `GROUP BY` / `SELECT DISTINCT` / hash-agg semantics for multi-row chunks.
entries.fix:
In `HashGroupKey`, avoid returning early on per-row encode errors that can be downgraded by `ErrCtx`.
- Continue encoding remaining rows, while recording the first (or aggregated) error to return after finishing the loop.
- For the time path, avoid overwriting `buf[i]` with `nil` if `EncodeMySQLTime` returns `nil, err` (use a temporary and keep the pre-existing slice content).
- Consider switching decimal group-key encoding to a lossless representation for `digitsFrac > 30` (e.g. `MyDecimal.ToHashKey()`/string-based encoding) to avoid truncation collisions, instead of clamping to 30.
entries.verify: Add an integration test that exercises multi-row hashing with a warning-producing decimal key, e.g. a query that produces multiple rows of `AVG(DECIMAL(65,30))` (so output scale >30) and applies `SELECT DISTINCT` over them, asserting all distinct rows are preserved. Also add a unit test for `HashGroupKey` ensuring it updates every `buf[i]` even when `EncodeDecimal` returns `types.ErrTruncated`.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1511`–`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1523`: in `HashGroupKey` (decimal path), on `EncodeDecimal` error it immediately `return buf, err` (same pattern for time at `pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1524`–`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1536`).
`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_util.go:149`–`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_util.go:157`: `GetGroupKey` runs `err = errCtx.HandleError(err)` and continues when the error is downgraded to warning/ignored.
`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_partial_worker.go:224`–`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_partial_worker.go:253`: HashAgg uses `groupKey[i]` bytes directly as hash/map keys (`murmur3.Sum32(groupKey[i])` and `mapper[...][string(groupKey[i])]`). Any rows left with empty/missing key bytes will be grouped/deduped incorrectly.
`pkg/util/codec/decimal.go:25`–`pkg/util/codec/decimal.go:34`: `EncodeDecimal` clamps `frac > mysql.MaxDecimalScale` to 30, then calls `dec.WriteBin(...)` which can return `types.ErrTruncated`.
`pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:274`–`pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:285` + `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_avg.go:84`–`pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_avg.go:108`: `AVG(DECIMAL)` can produce `retTp.decimal = old.decimal + div_precision_increment` (>30) and final result is rounded to that `frac`, so `MyDecimal` can have `digitsFrac > 30`.
The added test demonstrates this path is reachable and warning is surfaced: `tests/integrationtest/r/executor/aggregate.result:2062`–`tests/integrationtest/r/executor/aggregate.result:2066` shows warning 1265 with raw `%s/%d` placeholders (consistent with returning `types.ErrTruncated` without args from decimal encoding).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `git show upstream/master:pkg/util/codec/codec.go` still returns early on encode error (`return buf, err`) in `HashGroupKey`. File history after this commit only includes unrelated changes (`6e98fdeda5` string/collator optimization; `96bdeae43c` join key prealloc), and `pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_util.go` remains unchanged in this aspect.

entries.subject: planner/core: update missing virtual columns in `update` and `insert` (#58401)
entries.what: Blocker: `resolveGeneratedColumns` can make `InsertExec.OnDuplicate` non-empty even when the SQL has no `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` (via `ON UPDATE` columns), causing normal INSERT/INSERT IGNORE to take the ON DUPLICATE execution path and potentially suppress duplicate-key errors (no-op update).
entries.impact: MySQL-compatibility and correctness: a plain `INSERT` / `INSERT IGNORE` into a table that has an `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` column and generated columns depending on it can incorrectly behave like `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` (duplicate-key errors suppressed; `INSERT IGNORE` may update instead of ignore). This can silently change application behavior and data consistency expectations.
entries.fix: Ensure generated-column `OnDuplicates` are only produced/propagated when the statement actually has `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`. Minimal options: (1) in `resolveGeneratedColumns`, only add `ON UPDATE` columns into `onDups` if `onDups != nil && len(onDups) > 0`; (2) pass `nil` for `onDups` when `len(insert.OnDuplicate)==0`; or (3) in `pkg/executor/builder.go`, append `v.GenCols.OnDuplicates` only when `len(v.OnDuplicate)>0`.
entries.verify: Repro idea: create table with `t1 datetime DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` and `t2 ... GENERATED ALWAYS AS (date_add(t1, interval 1 day)) VIRTUAL` plus a UNIQUE/PK; insert one row; then run a plain duplicate insert without `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` and assert it errors with duplicate key. Also check `INSERT IGNORE` duplicate remains ignored (no update).
entries.evidence: Planner marks `ON UPDATE` columns as “in on-duplicate list” unconditionally in `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3955-3959` (writes `onDups[column.Name.L] = struct{}{}`) even when the SQL has no `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` (because `resolveOnDuplicate` always returns a non-nil map: `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:4139-4141`). Generated columns depending on those `ON UPDATE` columns then get appended to `igc.OnDuplicates` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3983-3991`). Executor builder always appends generated-column OnDuplicates into executor OnDuplicate: `pkg/executor/builder.go:1045-1048`. Insert executor switches behavior purely on `len(e.OnDuplicate)>0`: `pkg/executor/insert.go:90-100`, so a normal INSERT can be routed into `batchUpdateDupRows`. On duplicates, if OnDuplicate contains only generated-column assignments, `doDupRowUpdate` evaluates no non-generated assignments (`pkg/executor/insert.go:465-475`), then `updateRecord` can early-return “no changes” without applying generated assignments (`pkg/executor/write.go:165-185`), meaning duplicate-key conflicts become silent no-op updates instead of errors/ignore.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` for this pattern; `ResolveOnDuplicate` still returns a non-nil empty map for empty `onDup`, executor still gates ON DUP behavior on `len(OnDuplicate)`, so this semantic issue does not appear to be fixed up to `upstream/master`.

entries.subject: planner: handle firstrow columns in aggregation predicate pushdown (#63059)
entries.what: Unsound aggregation predicate pushdown for `FIRST_ROW` output columns: predicates on `FIRST_ROW`/`ANY_VALUE` outputs can be pushed below aggregation, filtering rows before computing other aggregates and changing their results.
