entries.impact: Blocker correctness: can silently change aggregate results (e.g., `MAX/COUNT/SUM/AVG`) by filtering rows *before* aggregation based on an arbitrary `FIRST_ROW`/`ANY_VALUE` column predicate, breaking SQL/MySQL semantics and producing wrong query results.
entries.fix: Only allow pushing predicates via `FIRST_ROW` outputs when the referenced `FIRST_ROW` value is proven group-invariant (e.g., its argument expression is in `GroupByItems`, or it’s functionally dependent on group keys via FD/PK/UK reasoning). A conservative stopgap is to forbid this `FIRST_ROW`-based pushdown when the aggregation contains any non-`firstrow` aggregate functions (because filtering pre-agg changes those aggregates’ inputs), unless group-invariance is proven.
entries.verify: Add a regression SQL case where a `FIRST_ROW`/`ANY_VALUE` predicate can exclude the row(s) contributing to another aggregate: `CREATE TABLE t(d INT, a INT, c INT); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,20,0),(1,10,1); SELECT d, MAX(a) m, ANY_VALUE(c) c FROM t GROUP BY d HAVING ANY_VALUE(c)=1;` Ensure optimizer does not push `ANY_VALUE(c)=1` below the aggregation (via `EXPLAIN`), and that any returned row has `m=20` (never `m=10`). Also cover the global-agg form `SELECT MAX(a) m, ANY_VALUE(c) c FROM t HAVING ANY_VALUE(c)=1;`.
entries.evidence: In `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_aggregation.go`, `splitCondForAggregation()` now does a second pushdown pass using `aggFirstRowColumns := expression.NewSchema(la.getAggFuncsColsForFirstRow()...)` and `pushDownPredicatesByAggFuncs()`. `pushDownPredicatesByAggFuncs()` pushes a scalar predicate down (and drops it from `ret`) if it references exactly one column and that column matches a `FIRST_ROW` output column, using `expression.ColumnSubstitute(...)` to rewrite it to the pre-agg expression. This is unsafe because TiDB’s plan builder appends `FIRST_ROW` agg funcs for *all* child columns: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go` (aggregation build) loops `for i, col := range p.Schema().Columns { NewAggFuncDesc(..., ast.AggFuncFirstRow, []{col}, ...) ... }`. Therefore many non-group-invariant, non-key columns become eligible for being pushed below aggregation. Counterexample (wrong results): with rows `(d=1,a=20,c=0),(d=1,a=10,c=1)`, query `SELECT d, MAX(a) AS m, ANY_VALUE(c) AS c FROM t GROUP BY d HAVING ANY_VALUE(c)=1` must never output `m=10` (if it outputs a row, `MAX(a)` is 20), but pushing `ANY_VALUE(c)=1` below the agg filters out `a=20` and makes `MAX(a)=10`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: `splitCondForAggregation()/pushDownPredicatesByAggFuncs()` logic is unchanged (no targeted fix in `git log d75dc0..upstream/master -- pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_aggregation.go`).

entries.subject: planner: fix nested IN expression rewriter bug (#63757)
entries.what: The fix only forces scalar-context rewriting for single-element non-subquery `IN` lists. Nested `IN`-subquery expressions used as a value still break when the outer `IN` list has more than one element: the inner `IN (subquery)` is rewritten with `asScalar=false` and produces no scalar expression on `ctxStack`, but `Leave` still calls `inToExpression`, which can index `ctxStack` with a negative offset and panic.
entries.impact: A valid nested expression like `((TRUE NOT IN (SELECT 1)) NOT IN (0, 1))` can still trigger an out-of-bounds/panic during planning (or an internal error if recovered), which is a stability/DoS risk and breaks SQL compatibility for nested IN expressions.
entries.fix: In `pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:580`, when `v.Sel == nil` and `len(v.List) != 1`, set `er.asScalar = true` before `break` so the IN-list’s children (especially a nested `IN (subquery)`/`EXISTS`) are rewritten as scalar values and push an expression onto `ctxStack`. Keep the existing `len(v.List)==1` unwrap logic so the `((subquery))` case still preserves the original `asScalar` when it is truly an IN-subquery. As a hardening fallback, add a stack-length guard in `inToExpression` to return an error instead of panicking when `stkLen < lLen+1`.
entries.verify: Add an integration test variant of the existing #63565 case with a multi-element IN list, e.g. `select 1 from tb0 where ((true not in (select 1)) not in (0,1));` (and `explain format='plan_tree' ...`). Verify it no longer panics and returns MySQL-compatible results (outer condition evaluates using the scalar value of the inner IN-subquery).
entries.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:923` rewrites each WHERE CNF item with `asScalar=false`. In `pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:580`, `*ast.PatternInExpr` only sets `er.asScalar=true` in the `len(v.List)==1` loop default (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:602`), but for `len(v.List)!=1` it just `break`s (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:586`) leaving `er.asScalar` as false at the root. An inner IN-subquery then captures `asScalar := er.asScalar` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1175`) and only appends a scalar result when `asScalar` is true (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1297`). The outer IN-list is still lowered in `Leave` via `inToExpression` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1617`), which assumes the stack contains `lLen+1` items and unconditionally indexes `er.ctxStack[stkLen-lLen-1]` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1977`), which can go negative if the LHS produced no scalar expression.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`; `Enter`’s `*ast.PatternInExpr` handling still leaves the `len(v.List) != 1` path without an `er.asScalar=true` assignment, and `inToExpression` still indexes `ctxStack[stkLen-lLen-1]` without a bounds guard.

entries.subject: executor: nonclustered partitioned table could miss updates due to duplicate _tidb_rowid from EXCHANGE PARTITION (#65084)
entries.what: Partitioned nonclustered tables: change disables the “skip multiple changes on same row” gate globally, so duplicate handles no longer suppress repeat updates; this can cause the same physical row to be updated multiple times (e.g., UPDATE JOIN duplicate matches) with stale `oldData`, risking wrong results and index inconsistency.
entries.impact: Potential correctness/data-consistency regression for nonclustered partitioned tables: the same row may be updated more than once in a single statement (UPDATE JOIN / duplicate matches), producing wrong final values and/or index-data inconsistency (stale index keys for intermediate values, false unique conflicts, incorrect reads).
entries.fix: Use a partition-aware dedup key instead of disabling dedup: for partitioned tables with int handles, track `(physicalPartitionID, handle)` (e.g., `kv.PartitionHandle`) in `updatedRowKeys`/`mergedRowData`/`matches` so different-partition rows don’t collide while the same-row repeat still dedups correctly. This likely requires propagating physical partition ID into the Update input schema (or deriving it reliably at runtime) and wrapping the handle only for the map key (and/or passing `PartitionHandle` through consistently).
entries.verify: Add regression coverage where a nonclustered partitioned target row matches multiple join rows with differing RHS values (e.g., `UPDATE tp JOIN s ... SET tp.u = s.u` with duplicates in `s` plus a unique/secondary index on `tp.u`) and assert (1) row is updated exactly once per matched row semantics and (2) index consistency (no stale keys / no unexpected unique conflicts). Keep existing EXCHANGE PARTITION duplicate `_tidb_rowid` case to ensure all partitions’ rows are updated.
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/update.go:92-132` sets `skipMultipleChangesOnSameRow=false` for `table.PartitionedTable` when `!tbl.Meta().HasClusteredIndex()`, and then forces `e.changed` to `changed && skipMultipleChangesOnSameRow` on duplicate handles (`pkg/executor/update.go:125-132`). This disables the executor’s existing “update each matched row once” gate (`if e.changed[i] { continue }` in `pkg/executor/update.go:273-281`) for *all* nonclustered partitioned tables, not just the EXCHANGE PARTITION duplicate-rowid case. If the same physical row is produced multiple times by the child plan (common in multi-table `UPDATE ... JOIN ...` with non-unique join matches), the executor can call `updateRecord()` multiple times for the same row while still passing the original `oldData` slice (`pkg/executor/update.go:289-313`). `TableCommon.UpdateRecord` rebuilds indexes by deleting based on `oldData` and inserting based on `newData` (`pkg/table/tables/tables.go:513-599`), so repeated updates with different `newData` can leave stale secondary/unique index entries from intermediate states (and can cause later false unique conflicts / wrong query results).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: no follow-up changes to this behavior were found (`git log 8227b493..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/update.go` is empty).

entries.subject: planner: derivePathStatsAndTryHeuristics can keep more MPP task (#65264)
entries.what: `derivePathStatsAndTryHeuristics` can append a nil TiFlash access path when MPP is enforced but the table has no TiFlash access path, leading to planner panics when later code iterates `ds.PossibleAccessPaths`.
entries.impact: With `tidb_allow_mpp=1` and `tidb_enforce_mpp=1` (or statement `set_var(tidb_enforce_mpp=on)`), queries on tables without TiFlash replicas (or replicas not ready) that hit heuristic pruning (common for point ranges / unique lookups) can produce `ds.PossibleAccessPaths` containing a nil entry and trigger a planner panic, causing query failures/outage.
entries.fix: Gate the keep/append on `tiflashPath != nil` (e.g. `if keep && tiflashPath != nil { ... }`) so enforced-MPP on tables without TiFlash paths cannot insert a nil `*AccessPath`. Optionally keep the warning behavior (via `RaiseWarningWhenMPPEnforced`) but avoid mutating `PossibleAccessPaths` with nil.
entries.verify: Repro/verify by planning a point-range query on a table with no TiFlash replicas while `tidb_allow_mpp=1` and `tidb_enforce_mpp=1` (or statement-level `set_var(tidb_enforce_mpp=on)`), and confirm the optimizer no longer panics and produces a sane fallback plan with a warning (if applicable). Add a planner casetest covering enforced-MPP + no-TiFlash-replica + point-range access path pruning.
entries.evidence: In `pkg/planner/core/stats.go:552-566`, `tiflashPath` is only set if a `kv.TiFlash` access path exists in `ds.AllPossibleAccessPaths`. When a heuristic `selected` path is chosen, `pkg/planner/core/stats.go:655-659` sets `keep := (PreferTiFlash || isMPPEnforced) && selected.StoreType != kv.TiFlash` and unconditionally appends `tiflashPath` (`append(ds.PossibleAccessPaths, tiflashPath)`) with no nil guard. But `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:1243-1249` shows TiFlash paths are not added when `tblInfo.TiFlashReplica` is nil or not available (it only calls `RaiseWarningWhenMPPEnforced`). Downstream code assumes non-nil paths and dereferences without checks, e.g. `pkg/planner/core/stats.go:424-440` (`getGeneralAttributesFromPaths`) and `pkg/planner/core/indexmerge_path.go:74-105` (loops over `ds.PossibleAccessPaths` and reads fields like `CountAfterAccess`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master`: `derivePathStatsAndTryHeuristics` still appends `tiflashPath` without a nil guard (`upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/stats.go` around lines 594-703), and `getPossibleAccessPaths` still omits TiFlash paths when replicas are absent/not ready (`upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` around lines 1275-1289).

entries.subject: planner: fix EXISTS subquery on cluster tables causing Column ID -1 (#65544)
entries.what: Cluster tables can now have `HandleCols == nil`, but the planner still records this nil handle in `handleHelper` as a `[]util.HandleCols{nil}` entry. `LogicalLock`/`PhysicalLock`/`SelectLockExec` assume handle entries are non-nil, so `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE/SHARE` on cluster tables can panic.
entries.impact: Blocker: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE/SHARE` involving cluster tables (e.g. `information_schema.tiflash_replica`) can panic during optimization (column pruning) or later in physical planning / execution due to nil method calls on `util.HandleCols`. This is a server-side stability issue (panic) and a potential DoS vector via crafted SQL.
entries.fix: Avoid storing a nil `util.HandleCols` element in `handleHelper` for tables without handles. Minimal: only add `handleMap[tableInfo.ID] = []util.HandleCols{handleCols}` when `handleCols != nil`; otherwise omit the entry (or store an empty slice). For stronger correctness, explicitly reject or ignore `FOR UPDATE/SHARE` on cluster tables (since they have no KV row handles) rather than building a lock plan.
entries.verify:
Run planning-only and runtime paths for locking on a cluster table and ensure no panic:
- `EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIFLASH_REPLICA FOR UPDATE;`
- `BEGIN; SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIFLASH_REPLICA FOR UPDATE; ROLLBACK;`
Also re-check the original regression still works:
- `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIFLASH_REPLICA);` and with a predicate.
entries.evidence: Cluster tables now leave `handleCols` nil in `buildDataSource` (skip ExtraHandleID path) but still push it into `handleHelper`: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4640`, `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4674`, `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4675`. `LogicalLock.PruneColumns` assumes every `util.HandleCols` is non-nil and unconditionally calls `col.IterColumns()` -> panic when `col` is nil: `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_lock.go:67`. The same nil will also panic in physical planning (`col.ResolveIndices`): `pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/physical_lock.go:107` and at runtime (`col.BuildHandle`): `pkg/executor/select.go:263`. Second confirmation that cluster tables like `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIFLASH_REPLICA` have no PK/common handle set (so `handleCols` can indeed be nil): only `CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY` sets `PKIsHandle`/`IsCommonHandle` in infoschema meta builder `pkg/infoschema/tables.go:423`, and `tableTableTiFlashReplicaCols` has no `PriKey` flags `pkg/infoschema/tables.go:1219`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): the same `handleMap[tableInfo.ID] = []util.HandleCols{handleCols}` pattern remains in `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go`, and `LogicalLock.PruneColumns` / `PhysicalLock.ResolveIndices` still lack nil-guards, so this issue does not appear fixed later.

entries.subject: planner, core: implement partial order TopN attach2Task and partial order flow (#65799)
entries.what: Partial-order TopN plan can produce wrong query results because the planner pushes a normal cop `Limit(count=Count+Offset)` on a prefix-index-ordered stream without any protocol/executor mechanism to include the extra rows needed for correctness within the boundary prefix.
entries.impact: When `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn=COST` is enabled and a prefix index is selected for `ORDER BY ... LIMIT`, the pushed-down index-side `Limit` can truncate the input to `Count+Offset` rows even though prefix indexes do not fully order by the column. This can return incorrect rows (violates ORDER BY semantics) for cases where multiple rows share the same indexed prefix but differ beyond the prefix length.
entries.fix:
To make this safe before executor/protocol support lands, do not push a hard `Limit` into `copTask.IndexPlan` for partial-order TopN (keep scanning and let a TiDB-side TopN short-circuit once implemented), or implement full plumbing:
- Encode partial-order truncation into the cop request (e.g., populate `tipb.Limit.truncate_key_expr` on newer tipb) derived from `PrefixCol/PrefixLen`.
- Add executor support to read `N + all rows with same truncated key` so the TopN sees a correctness-preserving superset.
entries.verify: Add a regression test that executes (not just EXPLAIN) with a prefix index and values sharing the same prefix but different full values, e.g. two rows where scan order-by-handle conflicts with full string order, and assert `ORDER BY col LIMIT 1` returns the correct row under `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn=COST` + `force_index`. Repeat for ASC/DESC and with OFFSET.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/planner/core/task.go:1356` `handlePartialOrderTopN` pushes `PhysicalLimit{Count: p.Count+p.Offset, PrefixCol: p.PrefixCol, PrefixLen: ...}` into `copTask.IndexPlan`, while `estimateMaxXForPartialOrder()` returns `0` (only used for stats).
`pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/physical_limit.go:153` `(*PhysicalLimit).ToPB` only sets `tipb.Limit{Limit: p.Count}` and never serializes `PrefixCol/PrefixLen` (same for `pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/physical_topn.go:205` TopN).
Integration test explicitly does not verify correctness yet: `tests/integrationtest/t/planner/core/partial_order_topn.test:441` (“TODO: Verify it after executor PR merged”).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`: `handlePartialOrderTopN` still pushes a `PhysicalLimit` and `(*PhysicalLimit).ToPB` still does not populate any truncate/prefix field (even though tipb has evolved).

entries.subject: parser,ast: support column masking grammar (#66031)
entries.what: New masking policy statements become parseable, but are not handled by planner/executor, so they can silently succeed without applying any masking (DDL) or return empty results (SHOW).
entries.impact: User-visible SQL (`CREATE MASKING POLICY`, `SHOW MASKING POLICIES`) can report success while having no effect (DDL) or returning empty results (SHOW). For a data-masking feature, this can create a false sense of protection and lead to sensitive data exposure. The planner also does not attach explicit privilege requirements for these new statements, which becomes a security issue once execution is added.
entries.fix: Until masking policy is fully implemented end-to-end, explicitly reject these statements (return a clear unsupported error) instead of silently succeeding. Minimal safety net: add a `default:` branch in `pkg/executor/ddl.go` to error on unknown `ast.DDLNode` types, and add either a `case ast.ShowMaskingPolicies:` implementation or a default error path in `pkg/executor/show.go` for unknown `ShowStmtType`. Also add corresponding privilege/visitInfo handling in `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` for `*ast.CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` and `ast.ShowMaskingPolicies` once supported.
entries.verify: 1) Execute `CREATE MASKING POLICY p ON t(c) AS c` and ensure it either creates the policy (and is observable) or returns a clear unsupported error; it must not silently succeed. 2) Execute `SHOW MASKING POLICIES FOR t` and ensure it returns an error or correct rows (not empty-by-default). 3) Verify privilege enforcement denies unprivileged users once supported.
entries.evidence: Parser adds `CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` grammar (`pkg/parser/parser.y:16183`) and the AST type is a `ast.DDLNode` (`pkg/parser/ast/ddl.go:39`). PlanBuilder routes any `ast.DDLNode` to `buildDDL` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:582`), and `buildDDL` unconditionally returns `&DDL{Statement: node}` even when the type-switch has no matching case (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5696`). `DDLExec.Next` has no case (and no `default:`) for `*ast.CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` (`pkg/executor/ddl.go:160`), so `err` remains nil and the executor returns success (`pkg/executor/ddl.go:248`). `ShowExec.fetchAll` likewise has no case for `ast.ShowMaskingPolicies` and falls through to `return nil` (`pkg/executor/show.go:181`, `pkg/executor/show.go:299`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): `CreateMaskingPolicyStmt` occurrences are still confined to parser/AST (no executor/planner handling found), and `pkg/executor/ddl.go` / `pkg/executor/show.go` still lack handling/default error for these new statement types.

entries.subject: privilege, server: support LDAP authentication (#43582)
entries.what: LDAP SASL auth method (`saslAuthMethod`) is read without synchronization during authentication, but written under lock via sysvar updates; this is a data race.
entries.impact: Concurrent `SET GLOBAL` / sysvar-cache rebuild can race with LDAP SASL authentication, causing undefined behavior (possible crash/panic due to Go data race), intermittent login failures, or inconsistent SASL mechanism use. This can manifest as a denial-of-service risk if sysvars are updated while LDAP SASL logins are in progress.
entries.fix: Capture the SASL method into a local variable while holding the existing RLock and use the local copy in the auth loop (e.g. grab `method := impl.saslAuthMethod` inside the closure and pass `method` to `ServerBindStep`). Optionally make `SetSASLAuthMethod` skip assignment when unchanged to avoid extra writes during sysvar-cache rebuilds.
entries.verify: Add a targeted concurrency test that runs `ldap.LDAPSASLAuthImpl.AuthLDAPSASL(...)` while concurrently changing `authentication_ldap_sasl_auth_method_name` via `SET GLOBAL` (or triggering sysvar cache rebuild), then validate under `go test -race` for the LDAP auth / server auth path.
entries.evidence: `privilege/privileges/ldap/sasl.go:66` reads `impl.saslAuthMethod` after releasing the config lock (`privilege/privileges/ldap/sasl.go:40`), while writes happen under `impl.Lock()` in `privilege/privileges/ldap/sasl.go:100`. The value is updated from sysvars (`sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:2522`). Sysvar-cache rebuild also invokes `SetGlobal` hooks for all global sysvars (`domain/sysvar_cache.go:128`), increasing the chance of concurrent writes during logins.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Still present on `upstream/master` at `pkg/privilege/privileges/ldap/sasl.go:66`.

entries.subject: *: unified the cancel/kill logic in tidb (#47063)
entries.what: BRIE kill monitoring uses `==` to compare the error returned by `SQLKiller.HandleSignal()` against `exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted`, but `HandleSignal()` returns a stack-wrapped error, so the comparison is always false and BRIE tasks won’t be canceled on kill.
entries.impact: `KILL QUERY` will not be observed by the BRIE executor’s polling goroutine, so long-running `BACKUP`/`RESTORE` via BRIE may not be cancelable promptly (or at all) through kill, potentially leaving heavy background work running and violating expected session/query cancellation semantics.
entries.fix:
Change the BRIE kill monitor to not use `==` on errors. Minimal behavioral-preserving fix:
- `err := e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().SQLKiller.HandleSignal(); if exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted.Equal(err) { ... }`
Safer fix (also cancels on max-exec-time / OOM signals):
- `if err := ...HandleSignal(); err != nil { bq.cancelTask(taskID); return }`
entries.verify: Manual repro: start a long-running BRIE `BACKUP`/`RESTORE` statement; from another session run `KILL QUERY <conn_id>`; expect BRIE statement to exit quickly and the BR task to stop (progress halts, no further work/logs). Add a regression test that asserts kill triggers `bq.cancelTask` for BRIE.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/executor/brie.go:552` compares `e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().SQLKiller.HandleSignal() == exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted`.
But `pkg/util/sqlkiller/sqlkiller.go:51-55` returns `exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted.GenWithStackByArgs()` / `exeerrors.ErrMaxExecTimeExceeded.GenWithStackByArgs()`, which (via pingcap/errors) wraps the base error with stack, so `== exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted` will never match.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on later history: `upstream/master:pkg/executor/brie.go:606` still uses `SQLKiller.HandleSignal() == exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted`.

entries.subject: executor: optimize (left outer) (anti) semi join which has no other condition (#47764)
entries.what: New `hashRowContainer.GetOneMatchedRow` can panic on hash collisions when the underlying `RowContainer` has not spilled, due to dereferencing `c.chkBuf` even when it is nil.
entries.impact: If a hash bucket contains entries that share the same 64-bit hash but have different join keys (a case the code explicitly handles via `matchJoinKey`/`probeCollision`), the first mismatching entry will trigger a nil-pointer panic in `GetOneMatchedRow`, aborting the join worker. TiDB recovers probe-worker panics into query errors, so this manifests as a query failure; in worst cases it can become a denial-of-service vector if collisions can be induced.
entries.fix: In `GetOneMatchedRow`, only compute/reset capacity when `c.chkBuf != nil` (spilled case). For the non-spill case (`c.chkBuf == nil`), skip chunk-capacity bookkeeping entirely, and guard the modulo/reset branch to avoid divide-by-zero. Keep collision counting unchanged.
entries.verify: Add a unit test alongside `pkg/executor/hash_table_test.go` that forces collisions (similar to existing `hashCollision`) and calls `GetOneMatchedRow` in non-spill mode; assert it does not panic and returns a matching row (or nil if none). Also run existing hash-table collision tests to ensure `probeCollision` remains tracked.
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/hash_table.go:156` (`GetOneMatchedRow`): after `GetRowAndAppendToChunkIfInDisk` assigns `c.chkBuf`, a collision path does `capacity = c.chkBuf.Capacity()` (`pkg/executor/hash_table.go:185`) and later `c.chkBuf.Reset()` (`pkg/executor/hash_table.go:190`) with no nil guard. But `GetRowAndAppendToChunkIfInDisk` returns a nil chunk when not spilled (`pkg/util/chunk/row_container.go:288`, return `..., nil, nil` at `pkg/util/chunk/row_container.go:299`), so `c.chkBuf` becomes nil in the common non-spill case. This fast path is exercised for semi/anti/left-outer-semi joins without conditions via `pkg/executor/join.go:925` (call at `pkg/executor/join.go:931`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on upstream/master (`b75374faa6`): the same nil-unsafe pattern exists in `pkg/executor/join/hash_table_v1.go:146` (uses `c.chkBuf.Capacity()` at `pkg/executor/join/hash_table_v1.go:175`), and `upstream/master` `RowContainer.GetRowAndAppendToChunkIfInDisk` still returns a nil chunk when not spilled.

entries.subject: types: fix issue that we can insert negative value to unsinged float column sometimes (#47946)
entries.what: `CAST(string AS REAL/FLOAT(M,D))` in expression layer no longer downgrades overflow/out-of-range errors to warnings (per StmtCtx flags) after the `ProduceFloatWithSpecifiedTp` refactor, causing SELECT/CAST to return errors where TiDB expects warning+clipped result.
entries.impact: Compatibility/correctness: `SELECT CAST('100' AS FLOAT(1,0))` (and similar string→FLOAT(M,D) casts, including UNSIGNED) can error out instead of returning the clipped value with a warning. This can break existing queries, and DML statements that explicitly use `CAST(...)` inside VALUES/SET may fail even when non-strict modes should only warn.
entries.fix: In both scalar and vector implementations of `builtinCastStringAsRealSig`, apply statement-context handling to the error returned by `types.ProduceFloatWithSpecifiedTp` (at least `StmtCtx.HandleTruncate(err)`, optionally followed by `StmtCtx.HandleOverflow(err, err)`), mirroring the approach in `pkg/table/column.go:296` so SELECT/non-strict contexts emit warnings instead of failing.
entries.verify: Add/extend expression tests that set a SELECT-like context (overflow/truncate as warning) and assert no error + warning emitted for out-of-range `CAST(str AS FLOAT(M,D))` (scalar + vectorized paths). Include UNSIGNED cases (e.g. `CAST('-1' AS FLOAT(1,0) UNSIGNED)` should yield 0 with warning, not an error).
entries.evidence: `builtinCastStringAsRealSig.evalReal` now calls `types.ProduceFloatWithSpecifiedTp(res, b.tp)` and returns `err` directly (`pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:1399`, `pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:1421`; vec: `pkg/expression/builtin_cast_vec.go:1684`, `pkg/expression/builtin_cast_vec.go:1695`). `types.ProduceFloatWithSpecifiedTp` returns `TruncateFloat`/overflow errors without any session-context downgrade (`pkg/types/datum.go:1004`). Unlike `table.CastValue`, which explicitly applies `sc.HandleTruncate(err)` and `sc.HandleOverflow(err, err)` to turn these into warnings when appropriate (`pkg/table/column.go:296`), this CAST path has no such handling, so overflow/out-of-range in `CAST(str AS FLOAT(M,D))` will surface as an execution error. This contradicts SELECT’s intended “overflow as warning” semantics (`pkg/executor/executor.go:2118` sets `sc.OverflowAsWarning=true` and `TruncateAsWarning=true`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go` still ends with `res, err = types.ProduceFloatWithSpecifiedTp(res, b.tp); return res, false, err`, and `pkg/types/datum.go` `ProduceFloatWithSpecifiedTp` still returns `TruncateFloat` errors without applying statement-context warning conversion.

entries.subject: types: fix the behavior of casting json string to integers (#48010)
modules: pkg/executor / sessionctx flags (AllowNegativeToUnsigned gating in write statements)
entries.what: Untrimmed sign detection in JSON-string->int conversion breaks negative values with leading whitespace, routing them through unsigned parsing and producing 0/overflow instead of the correct negative/wrapped result.
entries.impact: Query correctness/compatibility: SELECT `CAST(json_string AS SIGNED/UNSIGNED)` (and any other JSON->int conversions using this helper) returns wrong results for JSON strings with leading whitespace before `-` (e.g., `"  -1"` becomes 0/overflow instead of -1 or max-uint wrap). Can affect predicates, computed columns, and index values.
entries.fix: Trim spaces before sign detection in `ConvertJSONToInt` JSON-string branch: `trim := strings.TrimSpace(str)`; use `trim` for `isNegative` and pass `trim` into `StrToInt/StrToUint`. This matches `builtinCastStringAsIntSig` behavior and restores pre-change handling for leading whitespace.
entries.verify: Add a regression test: store JSON string with leading spaces (e.g., `insert into t(a) values ('"  -1"');`) and verify `select cast(a as signed), cast(a as unsigned)` matches string-cast semantics (-1 / 18446744073709551615) in SELECT; also verify write-context behavior if applicable (INSERT into unsigned column).
entries.evidence: `pkg/types/convert.go:632-640` computes `isNegative` on the raw JSON string without trimming whitespace; for JSON string values like `"  -1"`, `isNegative` is false and the code calls `StrToUint(...)`. `StrToUint` trims spaces but rejects negative prefixes except `-000*` (`pkg/types/convert.go:290-315`), so `"  -1"` becomes overflow->0. This contradicts the intended “consistent with casting a string” behavior and differs from the string CAST implementation, which trims before sign detection (`pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:1360-1364`). Regression vs first parent: `a565692...:pkg/types/convert.go:633-638` directly called `StrToInt/StrToUint`, both of which trim spaces internally, so leading-space negatives worked.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): the JSON-string path in `pkg/types/convert.go` still checks `str[0]=='-'` without trimming first; no later fix found.

entries.subject: parser/executor: admin show/set bdr role (#48504)
entries.what: `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` is misclassified as non-read-only, so it is blocked in cluster read-only modes.
entries.impact: When `RestrictedReadOnly`/`TiDBSuperReadOnly` is enabled, `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` will be rejected with `ErrSQLInReadOnlyMode` even though it performs no writes, blocking operators from querying cluster BDR role under read-only deployments.
entries.fix: Include `AdminShowBDRRole` in the read-only AdminStmt cases (in this commit’s layout, add it to the whitelist in `pkg/parser/ast/util.go:58`). Alternatively, special-case `*ast.AdminStmt` read-only SHOW variants in `allowInReadOnlyMode`.
entries.verify: Enable restricted/super read-only mode (e.g. set the corresponding global knobs) and execute `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE`; it should succeed and return 1 row. Also verify `ADMIN SET BDR ROLE ...` remains blocked without `RESTRICTED_REPLICA_WRITER_ADMIN` in read-only mode.
entries.evidence: `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` is a read-only admin command (planner builds `*plannercore.AdminShowBDRRole`, executor reads meta only), but it is not included in the AdminStmt read-only whitelist: `pkg/parser/ast/util.go:58` (switch lists `AdminShowTelemetry/AdminShowDDL/...` but not `AdminShowBDRRole`). Read-only mode enforcement blocks statements not allowed/read-only: `pkg/planner/optimize.go:153` calls `allowInReadOnlyMode`, which falls back to `IsReadOnly(node, vars)` for non-`*ast.ShowStmt` etc (`pkg/planner/optimize.go:417`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: `git show upstream/master:pkg/parser/ast/util.go` still whitelists only `AdminShowDDL/AdminShowDDLJobs/AdminShowSlow/...` and still excludes `AdminShowBDRRole` (see snippet around `upstream/master:pkg/parser/ast/util.go` line 65 in the shown output). Read-only gating remains based on read-only classification (`git show upstream/master:pkg/planner/optimize.go` shows the same allow-list + read-only fallback).

entries.subject: parser/executor: admin show/set bdr role (#48504)
entries.what: `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` executor is not retry-safe: it appends rows inside a retryable `RunInNewTxn` closure, risking duplicated output on internal txn retry.
entries.impact: If `RunInNewTxn` retries after the closure has appended once (e.g. commit retryable error or `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn=retry_once`), `req.AppendString` can run multiple times in a single `Next` call, yielding duplicate rows (or leaving `e.done=true` on an eventual error path), violating SQL result semantics.
entries.fix: Make the `RunInNewTxn` closure side-effect-free w.r.t. result materialization: read `role` into a local variable inside the closure, return nil, then append to `req` and set `e.done` after `RunInNewTxn` returns success. (Or pass `retryable=false` if retries are unnecessary for this read-only path.)
entries.verify: With failpoints enabled, set `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn=retry_once` and run `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE`; it should still return exactly one row. Also validate behavior under injected retryable commit errors (no duplicated rows).
entries.evidence: `AdminShowBDRRoleExec.Next` mutates output (`req.AppendString`) and executor state (`e.done=true`) inside a retryable `kv.RunInNewTxn(..., true, ...)` closure: `pkg/executor/executor.go:2764`. `kv.RunInNewTxn` can re-run the closure after a successful `f` when commit hits retryable errors / the `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn` failpoint: `pkg/kv/txn.go:106` (loop + failpoint at `pkg/kv/txn.go:146` + retry path at `pkg/kv/txn.go:166`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: the executor moved to `pkg/executor/show_bdr_role.go` but still appends to `req` and sets `done` inside the `RunInNewTxn(..., true, ...)` closure (`git show upstream/master:pkg/executor/show_bdr_role.go`, see lines around 42–51 in the shown output). `RunInNewTxn` still retries closure+commit and still has `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn` failpoint (`git show upstream/master:pkg/kv/txn.go`).

entries.subject: *: support serialization and deserialization of aggregate function for spill (#46632)
entries.what: Spill serialization for `JSON_ARRAYAGG`/`JSON_OBJECTAGG` cannot handle SQL NULL (represented as `nil`), because the `interface{}` serializer/deserializer has no `nil` encoding. This makes spill paths for these aggregates crash/fail when NULLs are present.
entries.impact: When hash aggregation spill is used with `JSON_ARRAYAGG`/`JSON_OBJECTAGG` and the input contains SQL `NULL`, spill serialization can panic (or abort the query via recovery), causing query failure under memory pressure and breaking correct JSON-null semantics.
entries.fix: Extend the spill interface encoding to support JSON null: add a dedicated type code (e.g. `NilType`) and handle it in both `SerializeInterface` and `DeserializeInterface` (encode only the type code; decode returns `nil`). Add unit coverage for `nil` entries in `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/spill_helper_test.go:836` and `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/spill_helper_test.go:886`.
entries.verify: Add a regression unit test that serializes/deserializes `partialResult4JsonArrayagg{entries: []any{nil, int64(1)}}` and `partialResult4JsonObjectAgg{entries: map[string]any{"k": nil}}` without panic and with exact round-trip. For end-to-end validation, run a query using `JSON_ARRAYAGG` over a nullable column while forcing HashAgg spill (low mem quota / tmp storage on OOM) and ensure it returns JSON `null` elements instead of error/panic.
entries.evidence:
`JSON_ARRAYAGG/JSON_OBJECTAGG` partial results explicitly allow `nil` elements/values: `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_json_arrayagg.go:78`, `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_json_objectagg.go:99`. `getRealJSONValue` returns `value.Clone().GetValue()` (NULL -> `nil`): `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_json_objectagg.go:137`. TiDB JSON builder treats `nil` as JSON null: `pkg/types/json_binary.go:656`.
Spill serialization iterates these entries and calls `SerializeInterface` on each: `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/spill_serialize_helper.go:150`, `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/spill_serialize_helper.go:158`. `SerializeInterface` has no `case nil` and panics on default: `pkg/util/serialization/serialization_util.go:175`. Deserialization similarly cannot represent `nil`: `pkg/util/serialization/deserialization_util.go:210`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (`b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`): `SerializeInterface` still lacks `nil` support and JSON aggs still admit `nil`.

entries.subject: expression: refactor like and ilike cache logic (#49676)
entries.what: Regression risk: switching `buildStringParam`/`buildIntParam` const-detection to `ConstItem(false)` makes ParamMarker-based params “const”, which in vectorized `ILIKE` causes in-place lowercasing of the pattern string. Because ParamMarker values are fetched from `PlanCacheParams` and strings/datums are zero-copy, this can mutate `EXECUTE ... USING @var` session user-variable values (and/or shared parameter bytes) as a side effect of evaluation.
entries.impact: Prepared statements executed via `EXECUTE ... USING @var` can unexpectedly modify the session user-variable value (e.g. `%C%` becomes `%c%`) when vectorized ILIKE is used, which violates expected session behavior and can lead to incorrect results in subsequent statements that reuse the same user variable.
entries.fix:
Avoid mutating ParamMarker/DeferredExpr-backed strings in place.
- Minimal local fix: in `pkg/expression/builtin_ilike_vec.go`, when `col == nil`, copy before lowercasing (e.g. `b := []byte(str)` then lower `b` and `param.setStrVal(string(b))`).
- Alternative containment: deep-copy datum bytes when putting EXECUTE USING values into `PlanCacheParams` (so later in-place mutations can’t affect session user-vars).
entries.verify:
SQL repro idea (no tests needed):
- `set tidb_enable_vectorized_expression=ON; set tidb_enable_prepared_plan_cache=ON; set @a='%C%';`
- `prepare s from 'select 1 where "x" ilike ?'; execute s using @a;`
- `select @a;` should remain `%C%` (no side-effect). Also try `prepare s2 from 'select ?, 1 where "x" ilike ?'; execute s2 using @a, @a;` to catch aliasing across params.
entries.evidence:
- `pkg/expression/builtin_func_param.go:81` now treats const as `bf.args[idx].ConstItem(false)`.
- For ParamMarkers, `pkg/expression/constant.go:425` makes `ConstItem(false)` always true, and `pkg/expression/constant.go:127` fetches the value from `sessionVars.PlanCacheParams.GetParamValue(...)`.
- Vectorized ILIKE lowercases “const” pattern in place: `pkg/expression/builtin_ilike_vec.go:108` uses `hack.Slice(str)` + `stringutil.LowerOneStringExcludeEscapeChar(...)`.
- Param/user-var strings are zero-copy backed by datum bytes: `pkg/types/datum.go:193` (`GetString`) and `pkg/types/datum.go:247` (`SetString`) both use `hack.String`/`hack.Slice`.
- EXECUTE ... USING user-vars goes through `getvar`, which returns `v.ToString()` without cloning: `pkg/expression/builtin_other.go:956`.
- Plan-cache params are stored by value without deep copy: `pkg/sessionctx/variable/session.go:1863` (`Append`) and `pkg/sessionctx/variable/session.go:1874` (`GetParamValue`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `pkg/expression/builtin_ilike_vec.go` still lowercases const strings in place; const-param detection still treats ParamMarkers as const-only-in-context; `PlanCacheParamList.GetParamValue` still returns stored datums without deep copy.

entries.subject: executor: fix pointGet and batchPointGet for global index (#47514)
entries.what: `Point_Get` on a global index learns the real partition physical ID only after reading the index value, but txn_scope validation runs only once (in `Open`) against the plan’s `partInfo` / logical table ID. It never re-validates txn_scope against the decoded partition ID used for the row-key read.
entries.impact: In non-global `txn_scope` deployments with per-partition placement policies, global-index `Point_Get` can read/lock a row in a partition whose leader DC does not match the transaction scope without raising the expected placement/txn_scope error. This breaks txn_scope/placement semantics and can lead to cross-scope reads (potentially inconsistent behavior under local-TXN assumptions).
entries.fix: After decoding `pid` for `e.idxInfo.Global` in `PointGetExecutor.Next`, verify scope for that `pid` before fetching the row key (and return `ErrInvalidPlacementPolicyCheck` with partition name on mismatch). Keep the existing check for the index key’s table ID if needed; the key point is to also validate the runtime-decoded partition physical ID.
entries.verify: Create a partitioned table with per-partition placement policies in different DCs, create a global unique index (so `Point_Get` uses global index), set session/txn `txn_scope` to DC_A, and point-get a row whose partition placement leader DC is DC_B; expect an `ErrInvalidPlacementPolicyCheck` (or equivalent) instead of returning the row.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/executor/point_get.go:188` calls `e.verifyTxnScope()` in `Open()` before any KV lookups.
For global index, `Next()` decodes the real partition ID from the index value and then switches the row key table ID: `pkg/executor/point_get.go:306-313` sets `tblID = pid` after `tablecodec.SplitIndexValue(e.handleVal)`.
But `verifyTxnScope()` only checks `e.partInfo.ID` when `partInfo != nil`, otherwise it checks the logical table ID: `pkg/executor/point_get.go:513-523`.
Placement bundles are keyed strictly by physical table ID (no fallback): `pkg/infoschema/infoschema.go:449-451`.
Contrast: distsql requests verify txn scope by extracting all physical table IDs from actual KV ranges: `pkg/distsql/request_builder.go:370-405`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream-master` (e.g. `upstream-master:pkg/executor/point_get.go`): it still performs `verifyTxnScope()` in `Open()` before decoding the global-index partition ID and does not add a txn_scope check after `pid` is decoded for the row-key access.

entries.subject: planner, statistics: support estimation for mv index access path (#49852)
entries.what: `expBackoffEstimation` regression: index-stats fallback can leave `selectivity` unset (0) on successful `GetRowCountByIndexRanges`, causing exponential-backoff selectivity/rowcount to collapse to 0.
entries.impact: When a column’s stats are missing/invalid and `expBackoffEstimation` falls back to other index stats (`coll.ColID2IdxIDs`), successful lookups will append a zero selectivity. This can drive exponential-backoff selectivity to 0, making interval range row-count estimates collapse to 0 and skipping the normal histogram fallback, leading to extreme underestimation and potentially severe plan/cost selection regressions.
entries.fix: In `expBackoffEstimation`, compute `realtimeCnt` and assign `selectivity = count/float64(realtimeCnt)` (or using the returned count struct) on the success path before breaking. Minimal change: move the `realtimeCnt`+`selectivity` assignment to immediately after the `GetRowCountByIndexRanges` call and before `if err == nil { break }`, or store the last successful `count`/`idxStats` and compute `selectivity` after the loop. Consider clamping selectivity to `[0,1]` and guarding `realtimeCnt==0` to avoid `0/0` NaNs.
entries.verify: Add a targeted unit test (planner/cardinality) that forces `expBackoffEstimation` to take the index-stats fallback: construct a multi-column range where a referenced column’s `coll.Columns[colID]` is invalid/missing but `coll.ColID2IdxIDs[colID]` contains a valid alternative index; assert `expBackoffEstimation` returns `success=true` and `sel>0` (and that `getIndexRowCountForStatsV2` doesn’t return 0 for a clearly non-empty range). Regression-check with the existing planner/cardinality tests around out-of-range and exponential backoff logic.
entries.evidence: In `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:456` the index-stats fallback calls `GetRowCountByIndexRanges`; on success it `break`s at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:457` before `selectivity` is assigned (only assigned in the error path at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:460-461`), then appends the still-zero `selectivity` at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:470`. First-parent behavior appended `count` then converted to selectivity later (`bf166d9^1:pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:452` and `bf166d9^1:pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:469-472`), so this regression is introduced here. Checked later history: the same pattern still exists on `upstream-master` (`pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:485-487` breaks before setting `selectivity`, which is only set at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:489-490`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: No fix found up to `upstream-master`; the same break-before-assign pattern still appears in `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:485-490` on `upstream-master`.

entries.subject: executor: refine sort spill (#48872)
entries.what: Spill-to-disk failures can be missed due to async error recording + unconditional `spillTriggered` transition, allowing external sort to treat partially-spilled partitions as complete and potentially return truncated/incorrect results without error.
entries.impact: If disk spill fails (e.g., out of temporary space / I/O error) after writing some chunks, the spilled metadata (`NumChunks`/`NumRows`) can reflect only the successfully written chunks. Because the partition is still marked `spillTriggered`, iteration can stop early and return a truncated result set without necessarily raising an error. In multi-partition merge, the current error-check strategy (only checking the last partition) further increases the chance of missing spill errors from earlier partitions.
entries.fix:
- Make spill failure unmissable and synchronous w.r.t. state transitions:
  - Record `spillError` inside `spillToDisk` while holding `syncLock` (or before broadcasting/setting `spillTriggered`), so any subsequent `checkError()` cannot race past it.
  - Only set `spillTriggered` when `spillToDiskImpl()` succeeds; if it fails, keep the partition in a non-spilled state (or force query failure) to avoid switching the read path to disk with incomplete metadata.
  - Optionally: have `getNextSortedRow()` return `spillError` early (under `syncLock`) to prevent silent truncation.
- Consider checking `checkError()` for every partition (or for the partition being popped) during external merge, not just the last partition.
entries.verify:
- Add a unit test that forces `DataInDiskByChunks.Add()` to return an error (e.g., via a failpoint / injected error) after some successful chunk writes, then assert the sort executor returns an error (and does not produce a shorter-but-successful result).
- Add a test for multi-partition external merge where a non-last partition’s spill fails and ensure the error is surfaced reliably.
- Manual reasoning check: ensure `spillTriggered` is only reachable when disk state is complete, or ensure any incomplete spill makes the executor fail fast.
entries.evidence:
- Spill error is recorded asynchronously *after* `spillToDisk` returns: `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_spill.go:53-60`.
- `spillToDisk` marks the partition as spilled (`defer s.setSpillTriggered()`) regardless of whether `spillToDiskImpl()` returns an error: `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_partition.go:250-258`.
- If `spillToDiskImpl()` hits an error during `inDisk.Add`, it returns early and does not free memory / repair iterator state: `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_partition.go:210-228`.
- `DataInDiskByChunks.Add()` only updates `offsetOfEachChunk` and `totalRowNum` after a successful write; on error the chunk (and its rows) are not represented in metadata, so later reads can silently see fewer rows: `pkg/util/chunk/chunk_in_disk.go:84-113`, `pkg/util/chunk/chunk_in_disk.go:309-317`.
- After spill is “triggered”, row iteration relies on `NumChunks()`/`GetChunk()`; reaching `restoredChkID >= NumChunks()` is treated as end-of-data (not an error): `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_partition.go:124-137`, `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_partition.go:261-285`.
- SortExec does not consistently re-check all partitions for errors during output; external merge checks only the *last* partition: `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go:177-183`. This increases the chance that a spill error in an earlier partition is never surfaced if the one-time `checkError()` happens before the async `setError()` wins the `syncLock`.
entries.later_fix_evidence:
Not fixed on `upstream/master` as of this review:
- `upstream/master:pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_spill.go` still sets `partition.setError(err)` asynchronously after `spillToDisk()` returns (see lines 56-63 in `git show upstream/master:pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_spill.go | nl -ba`).
- `upstream/master:pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go` still only checks the last partition error in `externalSorting` (see lines 497-503 in `git show upstream/master:pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go | nl -ba`).

entries.subject: importinto: executor part of import from select (#50341)
entries.what: `IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT` does not pin a single statement timestamp across parallel encoding workers, so `NOW()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`-based defaults / generated columns / `SET` clause expressions can evaluate to different times within the same statement when `WITH thread > 1`.
entries.impact:
Correctness/SQL-semantics drift for time-dependent expressions under parallel import-from-select.
- If a target column is omitted and has default `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`/`CURRENT_DATE` (or a generated column / `SET` clause expression uses `NOW()`/`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`), different worker encoders can observe different per-session “statement time”, so rows in the same statement can get different timestamps.
- This violates TiDB’s own stated invariant that `current_time` is constant within one SQL statement (`getStmtTimestamp`) and can lead to subtle data inconsistencies (especially noticeable when `WITH thread > 1`).
entries.fix:
Pin a single statement timestamp for the whole `IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT` execution and feed it into all KV encoders.
- Minimal: in `ImportSelectedRows`, compute one `ts := time.Now().Unix()` and set `chunkCheckpoint.Timestamp = ts` before calling `ProcessChunk` (or set a shared timestamp field on `TableImporter/LoadDataController` and have `getKVEncoder` fall back to it when `chunk.Timestamp==0`).
- Better semantic match: derive the timestamp from the user statement’s “now” (the same one used by the SQL layer) and propagate that exact value into all encoding sessions.
This ensures `NOW()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` used by defaults, generated columns, or `SET` clause evaluates consistently across worker goroutines when `WITH thread > 1`.
entries.verify:
Manual repro:
1) `create table src(id int); insert into src values (1),(2),(3),(4);`
2) `create table dst(id int, ts timestamp default current_timestamp);`
3) `import into dst(id) from select id from src with thread = 8;`
4) `select count(distinct ts) from dst;` Expect `1` if statement-time is pinned; >1 indicates per-worker divergence.
Also test `SET` clause: `import into dst(id) set ts = now() from select id from src with thread = 8;` and assert `count(distinct ts)=1`.
entries.evidence:
`IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT` fan-outs encoding across `ti.ThreadCnt` workers, each creating its own KV-encoding session with `Timestamp` coming from an empty `checkpoints.ChunkCheckpoint{}`.
- Query path uses `chunkCheckpoint := checkpoints.ChunkCheckpoint{}` (Timestamp defaults to 0): `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:699`.
- KV encoder uses `encode.SessionOptions{Timestamp: chunk.Timestamp}`: `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:355`.
- When the session sysvar `timestamp` is `DefTimestamp ("0")`, TiDB resolves it to a per-session cached `time.Now()` (statement cache): `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:93`.
- Time-dependent evaluation (e.g. `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `NOW()`) is supposed to be stable “during one sql statement”: `pkg/expression/helper.go:159` (`getStmtTimestamp`).
Second confirmation (contrast with file import): file-import pins a single timestamp across all chunks (`timestamp := time.Now().Unix()` and stored into `ChunkCheckpoint.Timestamp`): `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:450`.
Later-history check: still present on `upstream/master@b75374faa6` (query path still doesn’t attach a shared timestamp to query chunks / checkpoints; encoder still uses `chunk.Timestamp`): `pkg/executor/import_into.go:305` (upstream/master numbering from `git show`), `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:364`, `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:722`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master@b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`: import-from-select still sends query chunks without an attached shared timestamp and the KV encoder still uses `chunk.Timestamp` from an empty `ChunkCheckpoint` (see `git show` line numbers: `pkg/executor/import_into.go:305`, `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:364`, `pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go:722`).

entries.subject: statistics/handle/usage: modify the `SessionIndexUsageCollector` to implement new index usage design (#50050)
entries.what: `collector.globalCollector.SpawnSession()` fails to propagate the global `closeCh` to `sessionCollector`, so `SendDeltaSync()` cannot observe closure and may block forever once buffers fill after the worker stops (notably via `SessionIndexUsageCollector.Flush()` on session close).
entries.impact: If any session calls `Flush()` after the global collector worker has exited (e.g., shutdown ordering or late session teardown), `SendDeltaSync` can block indefinitely once the buffered `highPriorityDataCh` fills (default size 10). This can hang session teardown paths and potentially stall shutdown/cleanup routines.
entries.fix:
In `pkg/statistics/handle/usage/collector/collector.go`, wire the global close channel into spawned sessions: add `closeCh: g.closeCh` in `(*globalCollector[T]).SpawnSession()`.
Optionally harden shutdown semantics by closing/draining data channels on `Close()` (or making `SendDeltaSync` return immediately when closed) and by checking `SendDeltaSync` return value in callers that currently ignore it (e.g. `indexusage.SessionIndexUsageCollector.Flush`).
entries.evidence:
`pkg/statistics/handle/usage/collector/collector.go:63`-`71`: `SpawnSession()` returns `&sessionCollector[T]{ timeout: g.timeout, dataCh: g.dataCh, highPriorityDataCh: g.highPriorityDataCh, lastUpdate: time.Now() }` but never sets `closeCh`.
`pkg/statistics/handle/usage/collector/collector.go:163`-`171`: `SendDeltaSync` does `select { case s.highPriorityDataCh <- data: ...; case <-s.closeCh: return false }`; with `closeCh` left as nil, the close case is permanently disabled.
`pkg/statistics/handle/usage/indexusage/collector.go:226`-`233`: `SessionIndexUsageCollector.Flush()` calls `s.collector.SendDeltaSync(...)`.
`pkg/session/session.go:2577`-`2579`: session `Close()` calls `s.idxUsageCollector.Flush()`.
`pkg/statistics/handle/handle.go:203`-`208`: `Handle.Close()` calls `h.StatsUsage.Close()` (closing the global collector) independently of per-session lifecycles.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`: `pkg/statistics/handle/usage/collector/collector.go` still has `SpawnSession()` not setting `closeCh`, while `SendDeltaSync` still selects on `<-s.closeCh`.

entries.subject: hint: refactor PlanHints (#50768)
entries.what: Skew distinct-aggregation rewrite no longer propagates the full aggregation hint set to both newly created `LogicalAggregation` nodes, so aggregation hints can be partially dropped/ignored when the rewrite triggers.
entries.impact: Compatibility regression in optimizer hint behavior under the skew-distinct-agg rewrite path (`tidb_opt_skew_distinct_agg` enabled and rule triggers): user-specified aggregation hints can be silently partially ignored (e.g., HASH_AGG/STREAM_AGG/MPP_* lost on `topAgg`, AGG_TO_COP lost on `bottomAgg`), leading to unexpected plans and potential performance regressions.
entries.fix: Preserve prior hint behavior by copying both fields onto both rewritten aggregations (or calling a helper like `CopyAggHints`). Minimal fix: in `rewriteSkewDistinctAgg`, set `bottomAgg.PreferAggToCop = agg.PreferAggToCop` and set `topAgg.PreferAggType = agg.PreferAggType` (and keep existing assignments). If the asymmetric propagation is intentional, add an explicit comment and/or warning explaining the remapping so it’s not a silent behavior change.
entries.verify: Manually verify with `tidb_opt_skew_distinct_agg=1` using `EXPLAIN` for a query that triggers the rewrite (single distinct agg) combined with each agg hint (`HASH_AGG()`, `STREAM_AGG()`, `AGG_TO_COP()`, `MPP_1PHASE_AGG()`, `MPP_2PHASE_AGG()`): confirm the resulting plan still respects the hint(s) as it did pre-refactor (no silent drop, and expected agg operator/task-type preferences appear in the plan).
entries.evidence:
In `pkg/planner/core/rule_aggregation_skew_rewrite.go` (`rewriteSkewDistinctAgg`), the refactor changes propagation of aggregation hints when rewriting into `bottomAgg` + `topAgg`.
- Before (first parent): both `bottomAgg` and `topAgg` were initialized with `aggHints: agg.aggHints`, so both inherited `PreferAggType` and `PreferAggToCop`.
- After (this commit): `bottomAgg` sets only `PreferAggType: agg.PreferAggType` (no `PreferAggToCop`), and `topAgg` sets only `PreferAggToCop: agg.PreferAggToCop` (no `PreferAggType`).
These fields are actively consumed in `pkg/planner/core/exhaust_physical_plans.go`: `PreferAggType` affects HASH_AGG/STREAM_AGG/MPP phase preference, and `PreferAggToCop` affects whether RootTask plans are enumerated / AGG_TO_COP behavior, so missing propagation changes hint semantics.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history on both `master` and `upstream-master`: `pkg/planner/core/rule_aggregation_skew_rewrite.go` still shows the same partial propagation pattern (bottomAgg only sets `PreferAggType`, topAgg only sets `PreferAggToCop`).

entries.subject: importinto: support import from stale read (#50852)
entries.what: `tidb_snapshot` write prohibition for `IMPORT INTO` is only enforced on the no-result executor path; `IMPORT INTO ... FROM 'path'` returns job-info rows and appears to bypass the `tidb_snapshot` guard, allowing writes in history-read mode.
entries.impact: When `tidb_snapshot` is set (history read mode), `IMPORT INTO ... FROM 'path'` likely still executes because it returns rows (job info) and bypasses `handleNoDelayExecutor` where the write guard lives. This violates the contract that history read mode forbids writes, and can lead to accidental/unsafe data modification under a session assumed to be read-only.
entries.fix:
Enforce the `tidb_snapshot` (and `tidb_low_resolution_tso`) write-statement restriction independent of whether the executor returns rows.
Minimal/surgical options:
- Add an early guard in `ImportIntoExec.Next` (both select/non-select paths): if `e.userSctx.GetSessionVars().SnapshotTS != 0` return the same error as other write statements.
More consistent/systemic option:
- Move the snapshot/low-resolution write guard to a statement-level check in `ExecStmt.Exec` based on `a.IsReadOnly(...)` (or plan type), so it applies to both no-delay and recordset-returning write statements.
entries.verify:
Add/extend a unit test similar to `pkg/planner/core/plan_test.go:726+`:
- Create a table `t` and a minimal import source (or mock the import path if needed).
- `SET tidb_snapshot = '<valid ts>'`.
- Execute `IMPORT INTO t FROM '...path...'` and assert it errors with `can not execute write statement when 'tidb_snapshot' is set` (or the chosen consistent message).
Also keep existing coverage that `IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT ... AS OF TIMESTAMP ...` works when `tidb_snapshot` is not set.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/executor/adapter.go:813-821` only runs `handleNoDelayExecutor` (which contains the `tidb_snapshot` write guard) when `toCheck.Schema().Len() == 0`. The `tidb_snapshot` guard itself is in `pkg/executor/adapter.go:980-992` and is not applied on the recordset path.
`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:4268-4270` sets a non-empty output schema for `IMPORT INTO ... FROM 'path'` (i.e. `ld.Select == nil`), so it will go through the recordset execution path.
`pkg/executor/import_into.go:110-189` shows the non-SELECT import path executes the import and returns job info rows, with no `SnapshotTS` check inside `ImportIntoExec.Next`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (b75374faa6): `pkg/executor/adapter.go` still only checks `tidb_snapshot` in `handleNoDelayExecutor`, and `pkg/executor/import_into.go` still has no `SnapshotTS`/`tidb_snapshot` guard; `IMPORT INTO` still has a result schema for non-SELECT imports.

entries.subject: executor: Support spill of parallel hash aggregate (#49074)
entries.what: Parallel hash-agg spill temp files may leak on early `Close()` (query cancel/timeout) because `Close()` can run concurrently with the fetcher goroutine and closes only spill files already registered in `spillHelper`; registration happens later in `fetchChildData` defer, and there is no guaranteed post-registration cleanup.
entries.impact: On canceled/early-closed queries where parallel hash-agg spill has created temp files, TiDB can leak temporary spill files and file descriptors (and associated disk usage). This can accumulate under repeated cancellations/timeouts and lead to temp-dir disk exhaustion or FD pressure, impacting cluster stability.
entries.fix:
Make spill-file cleanup robust to `Close()` racing with `fetchChildData()`:
- Option A: ensure `Close()` waits for the fetcher goroutine to finish its defer (or at least for spill-file registration) before calling `spillHelper.close()`.
- Option B: in `Close()`, also close any `partialWorkers[i].spilledChunksIO` that exist (being careful to avoid double-closing; may require making `DataInDiskByChunks.Close()` idempotent or clearing references after closing).
- Option C: in `fetchChildData` defer, if `finishCh` is closed (cancellation), close spilled `DataInDiskByChunks` directly instead of relying on `Close()` after registration.
entries.verify: Repro-style validation (no tests required): run a query that triggers parallel hash-agg spill (low `tidb_mem_quota_query`, ensure tmp-storage-on-OOM path enabled), then cancel/kill the query mid-execution so `Close()` runs before normal completion. Observe whether spill temp files remain under TiDB temp dir and whether `StmtCtx.DiskTracker`/OS disk usage does not drop after cancellation.
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/internal/exec/executor.go:60` documents `Close()` may run concurrently with `Next()`. In this commit, parallel-hashagg spill files are only registered into the helper in the fetcher goroutine defer: `pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:420`-`440` (notably `addListInDisks` at `pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:428`-`435`). Cleanup in `Close()` only calls `spillHelper.close()` (`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:209`-`213`), which closes only `spillHelper.lock.spilledChunksIO` (`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_spill.go:107`-`115`). If `Close()` happens before the fetcher defer runs and registers `partialWorkers[i].spilledChunksIO`, those `DataInDiskByChunks` can remain open/unremoved.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943` (2026-03-20): `addListInDisks` still happens in `fetchChildData` defer (`upstream/master:pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:465`-`474`), while `Close()` still calls `spillHelper.close()` (`upstream/master:pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:205`-`238`). No synchronization/cleanup was found that guarantees spill files registered after `Close()` are closed.

entries.subject: util: Adjust binary collate behavior to do pattern matching in bytes (#51113)
entries.what: Privilege wildcard matching for `mysql.db.DB` (utf8mb4) is changed to byte-wise (`DoMatchBinary`), so `_` matches 1 byte instead of 1 UTF-8 character; this can cause incorrect privilege DB-pattern matches for multibyte database names.
entries.impact: Privilege DB-scope matching can diverge from MySQL/TiDB intended UTF-8 semantics for non-ASCII identifiers, potentially granting privileges to unintended databases (overmatch) or denying intended ones (undermatch) when patterns contain `_`/`%` and DB names contain multibyte characters.
entries.fix: For privilege DB/Host wildcard matching, use UTF-8 character-based matching (rune-based) instead of `DoMatchBinary`: store compiled pattern as `[]rune` + `patTypes` (like `derivedBinPattern`), or add a UTF-8-aware wildcard matcher for privilege patterns that treats `_` as one character (and is compatible with utf8mb4).
entries.verify: Add a privilege regression test using a multibyte DB name and wildcard patterns in `mysql.db` (via GRANT or direct row insert + privilege reload): ensure `_` counts characters (e.g., `"__%"` should not match a 1-character DB name like `"你"` under utf8mb4 semantics), while binary string LIKE behavior for BLOB/VARBINARY remains byte-wise (Issue50393-style case).
entries.evidence: `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go` switches Host/DB wildcard compilation+match to `stringutil.CompilePatternBinary` + `stringutil.DoMatchBinary`. `pkg/util/stringutil/string_util.go` implements these via `[]byte(str)`/`[]byte(pattern)` and `CompilePatternInnerBinary`/`doMatchInner`, so `_` (PatOne) matches **1 byte**, not 1 UTF-8 character. But `mysql.db.DB` is defined as `CHAR(64) CHARSET utf8mb4` (see `pkg/session/bootstrap.go` `CreateDBPrivTable`), so DB names/patterns are UTF-8. Byte-wise wildcard matching can overmatch vs character-wise semantics (e.g., pattern `"__%"` can match a 1-character DB name like `"你"` because it is 3 bytes: `_`+`_` consume 2 bytes and `%` consumes the last byte). Collation code also suggests byte-wise matching is intended only for collation `"binary"` (`pkg/util/collate/collate.go` maps `"binary"` to `binCollator{}` while utf8*_bin use derived/rune patterns).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go` still uses `CompilePatternBinary`/`DoMatchBinary` for Host/DB pattern matching; no follow-up correction found.

entries.subject: sessionctx,executor: support div_precision_increment sysvar (#51538)
entries.what: Plan cache correctness hole: `div_precision_increment` affects DECIMAL division/AVG type inference and rounding, but is not part of the plan cache key and `SET div_precision_increment` does not invalidate the session plan cache. Cached plans can therefore produce stale precision/rounding after the sysvar changes.
entries.impact: With plan cache enabled (prepared plan cache is default-on), if `div_precision_increment` changes after a statement’s plan is cached, cached expressions/agg funcs can keep stale return types and rounding rules, leading to silent incorrect precision/rounding (and potentially mismatched result metadata) for DECIMAL division and AVG. This creates correctness/compatibility differences between plan-cache hit vs miss and between plan-cache on/off.
entries.fix: Include `div_precision_increment` in the plan cache key (prepared + non-prepared), or explicitly invalidate/clear the session plan cache when `div_precision_increment` changes. Alternative (more invasive): on plan-cache hit, re-infer affected expression/agg return types (DECIMAL `/`, AVG retTp) using current session vars before building executors / pushdown expressions.
entries.verify:
- Repro (prepared plan cache): `prepare s from 'select a/b, avg(a/b) from t'; execute s; set div_precision_increment=10; execute s;` and compare with `set tidb_enable_prepared_plan_cache=0` (expect precision/scale to follow the new sysvar).
- Also test lowering the var (e.g. `set div_precision_increment=0`) to catch the `/` path that pads/rounds using cached `tp.GetDecimal()`.
- Add a regression test covering plan-cache hit behavior across `SET div_precision_increment`.
entries.evidence:
- Plan cache key does not include `div_precision_increment`: `pkg/planner/core/plan_cache_utils.go:304` (key uses `sessionVars.SQLMode`, `TimeZone`, etc., but no `DivPrecisionIncrement`).
- `/` DECIMAL return type is bound at build-time using the sysvar: `pkg/expression/builtin_arithmetic.go:664` (`setType4DivDecimal(..., ctx.GetSessionVars().GetDivPrecisionIncrement())`).
- Runtime division uses current sysvar but may round/pad using the cached type decimal: `pkg/expression/builtin_arithmetic.go:717` (uses `GetDivPrecisionIncrement()`), then `pkg/expression/builtin_arithmetic.go:725` rounds to `s.baseBuiltinFunc.tp.GetDecimal()`.
- AVG finalization uses current sysvar but rounds using cached `retTp` (inferred from the sysvar at plan-build time): `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_avg.go:92` (uses `GetDivPrecisionIncrement()`), then `pkg/executor/aggfuncs/func_avg.go:99` rounds to `e.retTp.GetDecimal()`, where `e.retTp` comes from type inference `pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:99` + `pkg/expression/aggregation/base_func.go:223`.
- Changing the sysvar via `SET` does not clear the session plan cache: `pkg/executor/set.go:218`.
- Prepared plan cache is enabled by default: `pkg/sessionctx/variable/tidb_vars.go:1375` (`DefTiDBEnablePrepPlanCache = true`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (current tip `b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`): `NewPlanCacheKey` still does not incorporate `div_precision_increment`, and `git grep DivPrecisionIncrement upstream/master -- pkg/planner/core` returns no matches (so no planner-side cache-key guard found).

entries.subject: txn: enable pipelined dml by hint (#51770)
entries.what: `SET_VAR(tidb_dml_type=bulk)` becomes hint-updatable but can leak into the next statement’s txn-mode selection because hint restores happen after `PrepareTxnCtx`, potentially disabling pessimistic-auto-commit for a subsequent statement.
entries.impact: Statement-scoped `SET_VAR(tidb_dml_type=bulk)` can unintentionally affect the *next* statement’s transaction mode (optimistic vs pessimistic auto-commit), changing lock behavior and conflict/error characteristics and violating expected hint scoping. This is a transaction/session behavior compatibility risk under default `tidb_txn_mode=pessimistic` + `pessimistic-auto-commit=true`.
entries.fix: Restore `SET_VAR`-affected sysvars before `PrepareTxnCtx` (e.g., move the restore step earlier in `ExecuteStmt`, or restore at end-of-statement instead of next-statement start). If reordering is risky, special-case `tidb_dml_type` so statement hints don’t persist in `SessionVars.BulkDMLEnabled` across statements before txn-mode selection.
entries.verify: Add a regression test with `pessimistic-auto-commit=true` and default `tidb_txn_mode=pessimistic`: execute a DML with `/*+ SET_VAR(tidb_dml_type=bulk) */`, then immediately execute another DML without hints; assert the second statement still uses pessimistic auto-commit (e.g., via a failpoint/log hook on txn provider selection or `kv.Pessimistic` option), proving the first statement’s hint does not influence the next statement’s txn mode.
entries.evidence:
- `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go`: `TiDBDMLType` sysvar now has `IsHintUpdatableVerified: true` and its `SetSession` toggles `SessionVars.BulkDMLEnabled` based on `tidb_dml_type` (standard/bulk).
- `pkg/planner/optimize.go`: `SET_VAR()` hints are applied via `sessVars.SetSystemVarWithOldValAsRet(name, val)` and the old value is recorded in `StmtCtx.AddSetVarHintRestore(name, oldV)`.
- `pkg/executor/executor.go`: `ResetContextOfStmt` restores `vars.StmtCtx.SetVarHintRestore` by calling `vars.SetSystemVar(name, val)` and clears the map; this runs at the *start of the next statement*.
- `pkg/session/session.go`: `ExecuteStmt` calls `PrepareTxnCtx(ctx)` **before** `executor.ResetContextOfStmt(s, stmtNode)`. `PrepareTxnCtx` decides txn mode using `PessimisticAutoCommit.Load() && !s.GetSessionVars().BulkDMLEnabled` and `TxnMode`.

Resulting leak: a statement with `/*+ SET_VAR(tidb_dml_type=bulk) */` sets `BulkDMLEnabled=true` and records a restore, but that restore is not applied until the next `ResetContextOfStmt`. The following statement’s `PrepareTxnCtx` runs while `BulkDMLEnabled` is still true, so it can start the next statement’s txn in optimistic mode (disabling pessimistic-auto-commit) even though the hint was meant to be statement-scoped.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master`: `pkg/session/session.go` still calls `PrepareTxnCtx` before `executor.ResetContextOfStmt`, and `ResetContextOfStmt` still restores `StmtCtx.SetVarHintRestore` (function now in `pkg/executor/select.go`), so this leak path still exists (not fixed later).

entries.subject: txn: save RPCs for Pipelined-DML (#51652)
entries.what: Potential semantic gap: pipelined DML switches lazy dup-key existence checks to `MemBuffer.GetLocal`, which ignores flushed (remote-buffer) mutations; this can miss duplicate-key detection across multiple flush generations in large/chunked inserts.
entries.impact: If an `INSERT ... SELECT` (or any chunked insert path) in pipelined mode triggers multiple flush generations and the input contains duplicate PK/unique-key values that span across generations, `GetLocal` may not observe earlier flushed keys, potentially missing duplicate-key detection and risking wrong SQL semantics and secondary-index/row inconsistency.
entries.fix: For pipelined transactions, ensure dup-key detection considers flushed mutations when needed (especially for `INSERT ... SELECT` / chunked execution): either (a) use `txn.Get(ctx, key)` / `txn.GetMemBuffer().Get(ctx, key)` instead of `GetLocal` for pipelined dup-key checks, or (b) use `BatchGet` to amortize remote-buffer lookups, or (c) maintain a per-statement “seen key” set for unique/PK keys to detect duplicates without extra RPCs.
entries.verify: Add a regression test that forces multiple pipelined flushes (low flush thresholds via failpoints + small chunk size) and runs an `INSERT ... SELECT` that produces duplicate PK/unique-key values far apart; assert it reliably errors with duplicate entry and leaves the table unchanged (and `admin check table` passes).
entries.evidence: In this commit, dup-key checks for record keys and unique index keys switch to `txn.GetMemBuffer().GetLocal(...)` when `LazyCheckKeyNotExists()` or `txn.IsPipelined()` is true: `pkg/table/tables/tables.go` (`TableCommon.AddRecord`) and `pkg/table/tables/index.go` (`(*index).Create`). `kv.MemBuffer.GetLocal` is introduced in `pkg/kv/kv.go` specifically to check only local memory. In the client-go pipelined memdb implementation (dependency updated by this commit), `GetLocal` explicitly does not consult flushed (remote-buffer) mutations, so keys flushed in older generations are invisible to `GetLocal`, while `Get/BatchGet` can see them via remote buffer. That makes correctness depend on an invariant that no duplicate key write happens after a key has been flushed and aged out of the local/flushing memdbs.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream-master`: similar `GetLocal`-based lazy dup-key checks remain present in `pkg/table/tables/tables.go` and `pkg/table/tables/index.go` (refactored under dup-key-check modes), so no clear later fix was found in TiDB history up to `upstream-master`.

entries.subject: *: Revert "add super privilege check for some admin commands (#51497)" (#51938)
entries.what: Privilege bypass: `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE` no longer requires `SUPER` because `buildAdmin` returns before appending the `mysql.SuperPriv` visitInfo, and the executor doesn’t enforce privileges either.
entries.impact: Any authenticated user (even with no granted privileges) can execute `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE` and toggle plugin state cluster-wide via etcd flush, potentially disabling audit/security/observability plugins or otherwise changing runtime behavior without authorization.
entries.fix: Re-introduce a privilege requirement for `ADMIN PLUGINS ENABLE/DISABLE` (at least `mysql.SuperPriv`) even if other admin commands are exempt. Minimal change: don’t early-return for `ast.AdminPluginEnable/Disable`; instead assign `ret = &AdminPlugins{...}` so the existing `appendVisitInfo(mysql.SuperPriv, ...)` at the end of `buildAdmin` applies. Alternatively, explicitly append an appropriate dynamic privilege / SUPER visitInfo before the early return.
entries.verify: Add/restore a privilege test that does not depend on any plugin being installed: create a user with no SUPER, run `ADMIN PLUGINS DISABLE audit`, and assert it fails at privilege-check time (e.g. error 8121 for `Super`). Also assert a SUPER user passes privilege check (execution may still error if the plugin is not present, but it must not fail with privilege error).
entries.evidence:
In this commit, `PlanBuilder.buildAdmin` returns early for plugin ops and bypasses the SUPER visitInfo append: `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:1445-1448` returns `&AdminPlugins{...}` directly, while `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:1476-1478` is the only place that appends `mysql.SuperPriv` for admin statements.
Privilege enforcement in planning depends on collected visitInfo: `pkg/planner/optimize.go:474-479` calls `core.CheckPrivilege(..., builder.GetVisitInfo())`.
Executor path has no additional privilege guard: `pkg/executor/admin_plugins.go:35-53` executes `plugin.ChangeDisableFlagAndFlush(...)` without verification.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed as of `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` still has early returns for `ast.AdminPluginEnable/Disable`, and `upstream/master:pkg/executor/admin_plugins.go` still has no privilege checks.

entries.subject: executor: Support parallel sort spill (#50747)
entries.what: Parallel sort spill triggered during result generation adjusts memory tracking as if input chunks were released, but keeps `sortedRowsIters` (and thus `chunk.Row` → `*Chunk`) alive until executor teardown, defeating spill’s purpose and potentially bypassing memory-quota enforcement.
