entries.what: `DROP STATS` may fail to reset cached table-level `StatsVer` to `Version0` when lazy loading skips creating any in-memory column/index stats objects, because `TableStatsFromStorage` now requires `hasStats` to perform the reset.
entries.impact: After `DROP STATS`, the stats cache can keep `table.StatsVer` as nonzero for tables whose stats objects were never loaded into memory (common with on-demand/lite-init paths). This makes the cache inconsistent with storage (`stats_ver=0`) and can lead to incorrect stats-version-dependent behavior (e.g. pre-#66772 auto-analyze’s `statistics.CheckAnalyzeVerOnTable` forcibly reusing a stale stats version, preventing expected version changes and violating `DROP STATS` semantics).
entries.fix:
In `TableStatsFromStorage`, decide whether to reset `table.StatsVer` based on the storage rows, not on whether any column/index objects were materialized in memory.
- Minimal approach: track `hasAnalyzedRow` while iterating `rows` (true if any row has `stats_ver != Version0`). If `!hasAnalyzedRow`, force `table.StatsVer = Version0` (covers `DROP STATS` even when lazy loading leaves `t.columns`/`t.indices` empty).
- Alternatively, compute `allZeroInStorage` by scanning `rows`’ `stats_ver` values and reset when they’re all zero.
entries.verify:
Add a regression test that exercises `DROP STATS` when no column/index objects are materialized:
- Use a table that can end up with empty `t.columns`/`t.indices` under on-demand/lazy loading (e.g. lease > 0, lite-init enabled, cold cache).
- `ANALYZE TABLE` to get nonzero `StatsVer`, confirm `StatsVer != Version0`.
- `DROP STATS` + `h.Update(...)`, then `h.GetPhysicalTableStats(...)` should report `StatsVer == Version0`.
- (Optional for older branches) set `@@tidb_analyze_version` to a different value and confirm version selection is no longer pinned by a stale `StatsVer` after `DROP STATS`.
entries.evidence:
In `pkg/statistics/handle/storage/read.go` `TableStatsFromStorage`, the post-load DROP STATS handling now only resets `table.StatsVer` when `hasStats && allZero`.
- `hasStats` is set only if `table.ForEachColumnImmutable` / `table.ForEachIndexImmutable` iterates at least one in-memory `*statistics.Column`/`*statistics.Index`.
- In the same file, `columnStatsFromStorage`/`indexStatsFromStorage` can return early without creating any column/index objects (e.g. `notNeedLoad` path when `col/idx == nil`), leaving `t.columns`/`t.indices` empty.
- `columnStatsFromStorage`/`indexStatsFromStorage` only update `table.StatsVer` when `statsVer != statistics.Version0`, so after `DROP STATS` (soft delete) they do not overwrite a previously-nonzero cached `table.StatsVer`.
- `pkg/statistics/handle/storage/gc.go` `DeleteTableStatsFromKV(..., soft=true)` sets `mysql.stats_histograms.stats_ver = 0` for the table, so the in-memory table-level `StatsVer` is expected to become `Version0` after refresh.
- The only `StatsVer = statistics.Version0` assignment in `pkg/statistics` is this `TableStatsFromStorage` block, so when `hasStats` is false the stale value can persist.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` version of `pkg/statistics/handle/storage/read.go`: it still contains the same `hasStats && allZero` guard before `table.StatsVer = statistics.Version0`, so this specific edge case is not addressed there.

entries.subject: ddl: sync affinity group for pd and support `show affinity` (#65049)
entries.what: `SHOW AFFINITY` ignores privilege/visibility checks and can disclose metadata for tables in databases the current user should not see.
entries.impact: Any authenticated user can run `SHOW AFFINITY` and learn DB/table/partition names across the cluster plus PD-derived topology-ish details (`Leader_store_id`, `Voter_store_ids`, region counts), even for schemas/tables they otherwise cannot see. This breaks the visibility model used by other `SHOW` statements and can leak tenant metadata in shared clusters.
entries.fix: Add privilege/visibility filtering in `fetchShowAffinity` similar to `fetchAllTablePlacements`/`fetchShowTables`: obtain `checker := privilege.GetPrivilegeManager(e.Ctx())` and `activeRoles := e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().ActiveRoles`, then skip any table where `checker != nil && !checker.RequestVerification(activeRoles, dbName, tblInfo.Name.O, "", mysql.AllPrivMask&(^mysql.CreateTMPTablePriv))` (and optionally also skip DBs failing `DBIsVisible`). If intended as admin-only, alternatively enforce an explicit (dynamic) privilege check in planner/executor.
entries.verify: Add a regression test: create `db1.t1` (affinity) and `db2.t2` (affinity); create user with privileges only on `db1`; assert `SHOW AFFINITY` does not include `db2/t2` (also for `LIKE`/`WHERE Db_name='db2'`). Manually sanity-check that privileged users still see all expected rows.
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/show_affinity.go:31-95` enumerates `domain.GetDomain(e.Ctx()).InfoSchema().ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute(infoschemacontext.AffinityAttribute)` and appends rows without any `privilege.GetPrivilegeManager` / `DBIsVisible` / `RequestVerification` filtering. `pkg/infoschema/infoschema.go:378-392` shows `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute` iterates all schemas from `is.AllSchemaNames()`. Contrast: `pkg/executor/show.go:570-611` filters `SHOW TABLES` via `DBIsVisible` + `RequestVerification`; `pkg/executor/show_placement.go:358-371` filters tables from `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute` via `RequestVerification`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99...`): `git log a14f0c8f..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` is empty and `git diff a14f0c8f..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` is empty, so this behavior appears unchanged.

entries.subject: sem, privilege: fix the issue that some privileges cannot be limited (#64160)
entries.what: SEMv2 restricted-privilege gating via `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` is bypassable with `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES` / `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES`: the code only checks whether the literal "ALL PRIVILEGES" token is restricted, and never enforces `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` based on the expanded privilege set that includes restricted static privileges (e.g. `DROP`, `FILE`).
entries.impact: SEMv2’s intended “restricted privilege delegation requires `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN`” can be bypassed by using `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES`/`REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES` unless operators also remember to restrict "ALL PRIVILEGES" in config. This undermines privilege-limiting policy and can allow delegating restricted static privileges without `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` in clusters relying on SEMv2 for security controls.
entries.fix: In `collectVisitInfoFromGrantStmt`/`collectVisitInfoFromRevokeStmt`, when `item.Priv == mysql.AllPriv`, expand `allPrivs` first and enforce `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN` if **any** expanded privilege is restricted (e.g. `if semv2.IsRestrictedPrivilege(strings.ToUpper(priv.String())) { append RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN visitInfo; break }`). Apply the same logic for DB/table-level ALL expansions.
entries.verify: Add a unit test extending `pkg/privilege/privileges/privileges_test.go:2226` (`TestGrantOptionWithSEMv2`): enable SEMv2, mark e.g. `DROP` (or `FILE`) restricted, create a user that has **all** required static privileges + `GRANT OPTION` but not `RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN`, then assert `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO grantee` fails with `[planner:1227] ... RESTRICTED_PRIV_ADMIN ...`. Add a similar `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES` case if revoke is also intended to be gated.
entries.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:4027` checks restricted-priv only against the raw `item` name/`item.Priv.String()`, but `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:4054` expands `mysql.AllPriv` into `allPrivs` and `break`s without re-checking restrictions for the expanded set (same pattern in REVOKE at `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3951` and `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3967`). `pkg/parser/mysql/privs.go:314` shows `mysql.AllGlobalPrivs` includes static privs like `DropPriv` and `FilePriv`, so `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES` can include restricted static privileges. `pkg/util/sem/v2/sem.go:186` shows restriction is an exact prefix/map check, so "ALL PRIVILEGES" being unrestricted does not imply individual restricted privs are gated.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `collectVisitInfoFromGrantStmt` still expands `mysql.AllPriv` without checking restrictions on the expanded privileges (see `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` around the function body starting near line ~3843).

entries.subject: planner: support cluster-level binding reload command (#65509)
entries.what: Potential panic in `SHOW [GLOBAL] BINDINGS` (and related SHOW) when binding cache returns nil entries: nil is checked only after sorting, but `sort.Slice` comparator dereferences binding fields.
entries.impact: If the global binding cache evicts entries (e.g., low `MemQuotaBindingCache` / memory pressure), `SHOW [GLOBAL] BINDINGS` can panic in `sort.Slice`, potentially crashing the session (and depending on panic recovery, risking process instability). `SHOW BINDING_CACHE_STATUS` can also panic when calling `binding.IsBindingEnabled()` on a nil entry.
entries.fix: Filter out nil bindings before sorting (or make the sort comparator nil-safe). Also add nil guards for other `GetAllBindings()` consumers like `pkg/executor/show.go:403-406` (`fetchShowBindingCacheStatus`).
entries.verify: Repro idea: set binding cache quota very small, create enough global bindings to trigger eviction, then run `SHOW GLOBAL BINDINGS` and `SHOW BINDING_CACHE_STATUS`; expect no panic and a stable result set (nil entries skipped safely).
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/show.go:344` sorts `bindings` and dereferences `bindings[i].UpdateTime` before any nil guard; the nil guard is only in the later loop (`pkg/executor/show.go:352-355`). `pkg/bindinfo/binding_cache.go:338-355` shows `GetAllBindings()` appends `c.GetBinding(sqlDigest)` which returns nil on cache miss (`pkg/bindinfo/binding_cache.go:339-342`), and notes LRU eviction can make cache state inconsistent (`pkg/bindinfo/binding_cache.go:368-370`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: `upstream/master:pkg/executor/show.go` still sorts before the nil guard (see `upstream/master:pkg/executor/show.go` around `fetchShowBind`, lines ~333-355 in `git show upstream/master:pkg/executor/show.go`).

entries.subject: planner: fix outer-join-to-anti-semi rewrite for nested outer joins (#65749)
entries.what: Scenario2 now uses FD-derived `NotNullCols` as a proxy for “inner column is NOT NULL”, but FD not-null can be inferred from null-rejecting join predicates inside an `innerChild` outer join even when the column can still be NULL in `innerChild` output. This can incorrectly enable outer-join→anti-semi rewrites and change SQL semantics.
entries.impact:
Potential wrong results: Scenario2 may become true for columns that are nullable in `innerChild` output (especially when `innerChild` is an outer-join subtree), causing `OuterJoinToSemiJoin` to rewrite an outer join into an anti-semi join and drop matched rows that legitimately satisfy `IS NULL` due to actual NULL values.

Example shape that can be mis-rewritten:
`SELECT ... FROM t1 LEFT JOIN (t2 LEFT JOIN t3 ON t2.i = t3.i) s ON s.j = t1.a WHERE s.i IS NULL;`
If `t2.i` is nullable and some matched `t2` row has `i IS NULL`, original query keeps that matched row; anti-semi rewrite would exclude it because a match exists.
entries.fix: Keep Scenario2 semantics “DDL NOT NULL, but not made nullable by outer joins” by gating FD-not-null with schema NOT NULL, e.g. require both `mysql.HasNotNullFlag(innerSch.Columns[idx].RetType.GetFlag())` and `fds.NotNullCols.Has(int(isNullCol.UniqueID))` (or otherwise restrict FD-based acceptance to cases that cannot be satisfied solely via join-predicate null-rejection inside an innerChild outer join).
entries.verify: Add a planner case test where the `IS NULL` column is nullable and comes from the outer side of a nested outer join, while the *top* outer join matches on a different (non-null) column. Assert the plan keeps `Selection isnull(...)` and does not rewrite the top join to `AntiSemiJoin`, and assert result includes a matched row with `inner_col IS NULL`.
entries.evidence:
- Scenario2 non-null check changed to FD-based: `pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_outer_join_to_semi_join.go:271-285` uses `innerChild.ExtractFD().NotNullCols.Has(isNullCol.UniqueID)` instead of `mysql.HasNotNullFlag`.
- Outer-join FD extraction treats join predicates as “filters” for not-null extraction: `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_join.go:916-952` builds `allConds` including `EqualConditions`/`OtherConditions`, runs `util.ExtractNotNullFromConds(allConds, p)`, then `filterFD.MakeNotNull(...)`.
- Not-null extraction marks *all referenced columns* of any null-rejected predicate as NOT NULL: `pkg/planner/util/funcdep_misc.go:24-50`.
- Outer-join FD merge keeps those NOT NULL markings for outer-side cols (only subtracts `innerCols`): `pkg/planner/funcdep/fd_graph.go:854-857`.
- In null-reject-check folding, functions with a NULL constant arg can fold to NULL even if other args aren’t constant: `pkg/expression/constant_fold.go:191-222`, making `IsNullRejected` true for many join predicates.

entries.subject: planner, meta: code preparation for the `_tidb_commit_ts` new hidden column (#65620)
entries.what: `_tidb_commit_ts` is treated as a globally reserved pseudo column name in planner/executor prep code via name-based blocking and pruning, but the reservation is enforced primarily at query-planning time (and by name), not by column ID or DDL-level prevention. This can break backward compatibility for any user tables that legitimately have a real column named `_tidb_commit_ts` (queries error out or the column is silently pruned/ignored).
entries.impact: Compatibility/SQL semantics risk: any existing user schema that already has a real column named `_tidb_commit_ts` will become effectively unusable in core DML/queries (SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE) because the planner rejects the column name outright and/or prunes it by name. Even without explicit reference, injecting an internal column with the same name into every `DataSource` can create duplicate-name edge cases that are then “handled” by ad-hoc name-based ignores/prunes (NATURAL JOIN, DELETE pruning, UPDATE column freezing).
entries.fix:
If `_tidb_commit_ts` is intended to be a reserved pseudo/hidden column name, enforce it at DDL time (CREATE/ALTER COLUMN name checks) so user tables can’t contain a real column with that name.
Additionally (defense-in-depth), prefer filtering/removing by column ID (`model.ExtraCommitTSID`) instead of `FieldName.ColName` where feasible (e.g., in the UPDATE projection cleanup), and return a more appropriate user-facing error class/code than `plannererrors.ErrInternal` for explicit usage attempts.
entries.verify:
1) On this commit, create a table with a real column named `_tidb_commit_ts` (if DDL allows), then run `SELECT _tidb_commit_ts FROM t`, `UPDATE t SET _tidb_commit_ts=...`, and `DELETE ... WHERE _tidb_commit_ts ...` and confirm planner errors/pruning behavior.
2) After implementing the fix, verify either: (a) DDL rejects such a column name consistently, or (b) user-defined `_tidb_commit_ts` behaves normally while only the pseudo-column is blocked/hidden.
3) Re-check NATURAL JOIN / `USING` / `SELECT *` behavior for tables around this reserved name.
entries.evidence:
Planner unconditionally appends an extra `_tidb_commit_ts` column into every `DataSource` schema/names: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4648`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4658`.
Planner then hard-blocks any SQL column reference by *name* `_tidb_commit_ts` in SELECT/SET-OPR/UPDATE/DELETE: `pkg/planner/core/preprocess.go:452`-`pkg/planner/core/preprocess.go:457`.
DML planning also removes/prunes by *name* (not by column ID):
- UPDATE freezes output columns then deletes any output named `_tidb_commit_ts`: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5497`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5502`.
- DELETE column pruning always clears any column named `_tidb_commit_ts`: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5261`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5266`.
NATURAL JOIN ignores `_tidb_commit_ts` by name when computing common columns: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:787`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:806`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked history up to `upstream/master` and found no evidence of a follow-up fix that removes these name-based guards or moves the reservation to DDL-level enforcement (e.g., `git grep` on `upstream/master` still shows the `ExtraCommitTSName` preprocessor guard and planner-side name-based removal).

entries.subject: planner: support straight_join() hint in CTEs and subqueries (#65696)
entries.what: `PlanBuilder.inStraightJoin` is no longer reset for SELECT blocks without STRAIGHT_JOIN, so once an outer SELECT enables STRAIGHT_JOIN (keyword or `/*+ straight_join() */`), nested SELECTs inherit the flag and have join-reorder disabled even if they did not specify STRAIGHT_JOIN.
entries.impact: Compatibility/semantics: STRAIGHT_JOIN becomes dynamically scoped across nested SELECTs, so subqueries/derived tables/CTEs inside a straight-join query block may unexpectedly preserve SQL join order and skip join reordering. This can change EXPLAIN output and cause large performance regressions for complex nested queries; it also breaks the comment-defined “current SELECT only” scope.
entries.fix: In `buildSelect`, always scope `b.inStraightJoin` to the current SELECT by pushing/unconditionally setting it to `straightJoinFromKeyword||straightJoinFromHint` (or that value OR'ed with any intended statement-level flag) and deferring restore, instead of only setting it when the value is true.
entries.verify: Add an integration test where the outer query uses the `SELECT STRAIGHT_JOIN` keyword (not the statement-level `/*+ straight_join() */` hint) and the inner derived-table SELECT has no straight_join; confirm the inner plan still gets reordered (i.e., outer STRAIGHT_JOIN does not affect the derived-table join order). Also verify existing straight_join-in-CTE/subquery tests still pass.
entries.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:3733` only pushes `b.inStraightJoin` when `straightJoinFromKeyword||straightJoinFromHint` is true, with no reset path; this contradicts the intended per-SELECT meaning (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:238`). Because the parser always creates a non-nil `SelectStmtOpts` even when empty (`pkg/parser/parser.y:10536`), the pre-change code reset `b.inStraightJoin` to false for each SELECT but the new code does not. The inherited flag marks joins as `StraightJoin` (`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:584`), and join reorder explicitly bails out on `join.StraightJoin` (`pkg/planner/core/rule_join_reorder.go:72`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go` still uses the same conditional `if straightJoinFromKeyword || straightJoinFromHint { ... }` block, so this behavior remains.

entries.subject: statistics: refactor out of range percent calculations (#65857)
entries.what: Potential NaN regression in out-of-range estimation: extracting overlap-percent math into helpers that use built-in `min/max` can propagate NaNs into `OutOfRangeRowCount` results when `histWidth` becomes NaN (e.g., `histL==histR==±Inf`) or range endpoints are NaN; the pre-refactor code largely avoided computing percents under NaN bounds via overlap-condition short-circuiting.
entries.impact: If `histWidth` (or inputs) becomes NaN, `RowEstimate.Est/MaxEst` can become NaN and propagate into planner selectivity/costing. `RowEstimate.Clamp` and `mathutil.Clamp` do not sanitize NaN, so this can yield unstable plan choice behavior and potential downstream panics/undefined comparisons in code assuming finite row counts.
entries.fix: Treat NaN histogram widths/inputs as “invalid for overlap percent” to preserve finite estimates: (a) in `OutOfRangeRowCount`, add `if math.IsNaN(histWidth) { histWidth = 0 }` before computing `boundL/boundR`, and/or (b) in `calculateLeftOverlapPercent`/`calculateRightOverlapPercent`, early-return 0 when any of `l,r,bound*,hist*,histWidth` is NaN. Either approach restores the prior effective behavior (NaN bounds → 0% overlap) and prevents NaN poisoning.
entries.verify: Add a targeted unit test constructing a float histogram whose bounds are both `+Inf` (or both `-Inf`) and assert `OutOfRangeRowCount` returns finite (`!math.IsNaN`/`!math.IsInf`) `RowEstimate` fields for representative ranges. Optionally add a regression test with NaN predicate bounds (if ranger can produce them) to ensure the estimate remains finite.
entries.evidence: `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1034` (`calculateLeftOverlapPercent`) and `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1058` (`calculateRightOverlapPercent`) bound inputs via built-in `max`/`min` and then compute a ratio dividing by `histWidth^2` (e.g., `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1047`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1052`). In `OutOfRangeRowCount`, `histWidth := histR - histL` is only normalized for `< 0` and `+Inf` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1158`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1166`), so `histWidth` can be `NaN` (e.g., `Inf - Inf`), making `boundL/boundR` `NaN` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1167`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1168`) and causing the overlap helpers to return `NaN` due to `min/max` NaN propagation (confirmed via `go doc builtin min` / `go doc builtin max`: “if any args are NaNs, returns NaN”). Those percents flow into `totalPercent` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1184`) and then into `avgRowCount` / `finalEst` / `maxEst` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1187`, `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1214`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1222`). In the parent version (first parent), percent computation was guarded by overlap comparisons (e.g., `...^:pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1128`–`:1161`), so `NaN` bounds tended to short-circuit overlap and keep percents at 0, avoiding NaN propagation.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` `pkg/statistics/histogram.go`: overlap helpers remain and there is still no `math.IsNaN(histWidth)` / input-NaN guard around overlap-percent computation.

entries.subject: planner, core: implement partial order TopN attach2Task and partial order flow (#65799)
entries.what: `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` changes from BOOL to ENUM and drops support for legacy `ON/OFF/0/1` values, breaking sysvar/hint compatibility across versions.
entries.impact: Compatibility break for existing automation/config/hints that set `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` to `ON/OFF` or `1/0`; these now fail with `ErrWrongValueForVar` (MySQL error 1231), potentially causing query failures on upgrade.
entries.fix:
If backward compatibility is desired, accept legacy bool values as aliases:
- Map `ON`/`1` -> `COST`
- Map `OFF`/`0` -> `DISABLE`
while still returning/storing canonical enum values.
If strictness is intentional, document this as a breaking sysvar interface change and consider keeping a deprecated alias sysvar for older automation.
entries.verify: Add/adjust unit tests to cover legacy inputs mapping to canonical values and ensure `SELECT @@tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` returns only `DISABLE|COST` while `SET ... = ON/OFF/0/1` remains accepted (if compatibility is chosen).
entries.evidence:
Parent (`995d6f987c5a...`) sysvar accepted bool forms: `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go` defines `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` as `TypeBool` and validates `0/1/ON/OFF`.
This commit changes it to enum-only: `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:3073` sets `TypeEnum` with `PossibleValues: ["DISABLE","COST"]` and validation rejects `ON/OFF/0/1`; tests assert these now error (`pkg/sessionctx/variable/tests/session_test.go:757`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`: sysvar remains `TypeEnum` and still rejects `ON/OFF/0/1`.

entries.subject: planner: simplify outer join other conditions (#66015)
entries.what: Outer join `OtherConditions` simplification can incorrectly eliminate evaluation of mutable/side-effect expressions due to constant short-circuit rewrites that ignore left-to-right eval order.
entries.impact:
Outer join `ON` conditions that include mutable/side-effect functions combined with logical constants can change observable behavior after this change.
Examples that can diverge from pre-change behavior / MySQL-like left-to-right evaluation:
- `... LEFT JOIN ... ON (sleep(1) OR 1)` could be simplified to constant TRUE and skip `sleep(1)` entirely.
- `... LEFT JOIN ... ON (rand() AND 0)` could be simplified to constant FALSE and skip evaluating `rand()`, which can change subsequent `rand()` results in the same statement because RAND() uses shared RNG state.
entries.fix:
Narrow the outer-join `OtherConditions` rewrite to avoid eliminating evaluation of mutable/side-effect expressions:
- Prefer a dedicated simplifier for outer-join `OtherConditions` that only removes *neutral* constants (`expr OR FALSE` -> `expr`, `expr AND TRUE` -> `expr`, double-NOT), and avoids annihilator rewrites (`expr OR TRUE`, `expr AND FALSE`) unless it can prove it won’t drop evaluation of a mutable-effects subexpression (or unless the constant is the *left* operand, matching short-circuit behavior).
- Alternatively, skip this simplification (or the “drop-other-side” cases) when `expression.IsMutableEffectsExpr(cond)` is true for the affected predicate tree.
entries.verify:
Add/execute targeted SQL-level regression checks that assert mutable-effects evaluation is preserved for outer-join ON conditions:
- Timing/side-effect: `select 1 from t1 left join t2 on (sleep(1) or 1) limit 1;` should still incur ~1s delay if left-to-right eval is required.
- RNG state: `select rand(), rand() from t1 left join t2 on (rand() or 1) limit 1;` should match behavior without rewriting away the `ON`-clause `rand()` call (seed-controlled variant if available).
entries.evidence:
- New behavior: `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_join.go:155-178` calls `ruleutil.ApplyPredicateSimplification(p.SCtx(), p.OtherConditions, false, nil)` for `LeftOuterJoin`/`RightOuterJoin`.
- That simplifier can drop the *left* operand when the *right* operand is a logical constant: `pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_predicate_simplification.go:440-455` (e.g. OR: `secondType == TruePredicate` returns `secondCondition`; AND: `secondType == falsePredicate` returns `secondCondition`).
- But runtime eval of AND/OR is left-to-right (so the left operand is evaluated first): `pkg/expression/builtin_op.go:104-111` (AND), `pkg/expression/builtin_op.go:161-169` (OR).
- TiDB explicitly treats functions like `rand()`/`sleep()`/time funcs as mutable/side-effect: `pkg/expression/function_traits.go:223-264`.
- Join condition classification intentionally keeps mutable expressions in `OtherConditions` (to avoid pushdown): `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_join.go:1499-1507`.
- Later history check: `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd` still contains the same `ApplyPredicateSimplification` call in `LogicalJoin.PredicatePushDown` (not fixed later).
entries.later_fix_evidence: No follow-up fix found up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`); the `ApplyPredicateSimplification` call on outer-join `OtherConditions` remains present.

entries.subject: *: implement shared lock for foreign key (#65752)
entries.what: With `tidb_foreign_key_check_in_shared_lock=ON`, FK checks acquire shared pessimistic locks on referenced keys; later statements in the same pessimistic transaction that need exclusive locks on those keys can fail because shared→exclusive lock upgrade is explicitly unsupported in client-go.
entries.impact: Enabling `tidb_foreign_key_check_in_shared_lock` (session or global) can introduce user-visible errors in valid multi-statement pessimistic transactions, e.g. inserting/updating child rows (locking parent rows shared) and later updating/deleting the same parent rows in the same txn. This diverges from MySQL/InnoDB lock/transaction semantics and can break workloads that toggle or globally enable the feature for concurrency.
entries.fix: Document and gate the limitation (warn/forbid enabling when workloads may later write referenced rows), or implement true shared→exclusive lock upgrade support in TiKV/client-go. A TiDB-side workaround would require a safe upgrade path (e.g. pessimistic-rollback shared lock + re-lock exclusive with retry), which needs careful correctness/atomicity design.
entries.verify: Repro SQL: `BEGIN PESSIMISTIC; SET @@tidb_foreign_key_check_in_shared_lock=ON; INSERT INTO child VALUES (..., parent_id); UPDATE parent SET ... WHERE id=parent_id;` — expect either success (if upgrade supported) or a deterministic/clearly documented error. Add a RealTiKV regression test covering this pattern.
entries.evidence: TiDB collects FK-check lock keys into TxnCtx as *shared* for pessimistic txns (`pkg/executor/foreign_key.go:256-263`, `TransactionContext.AddUnchangedKeyForLock(k, true)`), and when the sysvar is ON it locks them in a second phase using `newLockCtx(..., shared=true)` / `txn.LockKeys` (`pkg/executor/adapter.go:1254-1277`). The client-go version pinned by this commit (`go.mod:127` => `github.com/tikv/client-go/v2 v2.0.8-0.20260209125252-1fd09ba3ef10`) explicitly rejects shared→exclusive lock upgrades: `.../txnkv/transaction/txn.go:1460` returns `"upgrading a shared lock to an exclusive lock is not supported"` (also asserted by `.../txnkv/transaction/txn_test.go:207-235`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: `go.mod` at `upstream/master` pins `github.com/tikv/client-go/v2 v2.0.8-0.20260316081220-602cdf086c43`, and that version’s `txnkv/transaction/txn.go` still contains the same `upgrading a shared lock...is not supported` error.

entries.subject: planner: fix IndexJoin with Aggregation correctness issue (#66217)
entries.what: The new IndexJoin+Aggregation correctness guard can incorrectly allow unsafe plans when GROUP BY items are expressions: it checks inner join keys against *columns referenced inside* GROUP BY expressions, not against the actual grouping key(s), so aggregation groups can still be split across IndexJoin batches and yield wrong results.
entries.impact: Potential wrong query results for IndexJoin+Aggregation inner multi-pattern when ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is off and GROUP BY items are expressions: IndexJoin can still split a single logical group across batches and emit multiple partial groups, causing duplicates/incorrect join results. This is correctness (result-set) risk, not just plan/hint applicability.
entries.fix: Make the safety check conservative for GROUP BY expressions: treat a GROUP BY item as “covering” an inner join key only when the GROUP BY item itself is a plain `*expression.Column` (same `UniqueID`), not when the key merely appears inside a scalar-function GROUP BY expression. Longer-term, implement the TODO and use FD/equivalence reasoning to prove join keys are functionally determined by the group-by key(s).
entries.verify: Add an integration case similar to the ones added in `tests/integrationtest/t/planner/core/indexjoin.test`, but with GROUP BY expressions that can collapse multiple join-key values into one group (e.g. `GROUP BY a+b`), with `@@sql_mode=''` and data where one group spans multiple `a` values. Assert `INL_JOIN` is rejected (warning 1815) or results match `HASH_JOIN` under forced small/batched outer-side execution.
entries.evidence:
In `pkg/planner/core/exhaust_physical_plans.go`, `checkIndexJoinInnerTaskWithAgg()` builds `groupByCols := expression.ExtractColumnsMapFromExpressions(nil, la.GroupByItems...)` and then only checks `InnerJoinKeys` (filtered to those present in the leaf `DataSource` schema) by `UniqueID` membership in that map. `ExtractColumnsMapFromExpressions` recursively extracts columns from scalar functions (`pkg/expression/util.go:extractColumns`), and GROUP BY items are kept as arbitrary expressions by `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:rewriteGbyExprs` (it only rewrites AST -> expression, no “GROUP BY expr -> new column” normalization). Therefore a GROUP BY expression like `GROUP BY (a+b)` makes both `a` and `b` appear “covered”, so an IndexJoin driven by join key `a` can still pass the new guard even though `a` is not a grouping key and aggregation groups can still be split across index-join batches.
A concrete counterexample class (ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY disabled): `t2(a,b)` rows (1,2) and (2,1) share the same group key (a+b=3); derived table `select a from t2 group by a+b` should yield 1 row total, but IndexJoin batching by `a` can produce 2 different `firstrow(a)` results in different batches, yielding a join result not representable by any single evaluation of the derived aggregation.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/exhaust_physical_plans.go` still uses `ExtractColumnsMapFromExpressions(nil, la.GroupByItems...)` and the same `UniqueID` subset test in `checkIndexJoinInnerTaskWithAgg()`. `upstream/master:pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go` `rewriteGbyExprs()` still preserves GROUP BY as arbitrary expressions.

entries.subject: importinto: introduce a param to control conflict resolution (#66701)
entries.what: `on_duplicate_key='error'` (default) can fail late in the global-sort write+ingest phase with no rollback, potentially leaving the target table partially imported and secondary indexes inconsistent because data and index KV groups are ingested in separate, unordered subtasks and conflict-resolution steps are skipped on failure.
entries.impact: If a duplicate is detected during `ImportStepWriteAndIngest` for an index KV group while some data KV subtasks have already imported row data, the task will fail and skip conflict-resolution steps; with no rollback, the table can end up partially imported with missing/partial secondary index KVs. After table mode is reset to normal, this can lead to wrong query results (index lookups missing rows) and incorrect constraint enforcement until the table is manually repaired/truncated.
entries.fix:
For `on_duplicate_key='error'` (especially default), ensure the job cannot leave the table in an index-inconsistent intermediate state on failure. Options:
- Add a pre-ingest “global duplicate check” phase that scans/sorts all KV groups and fails before any `ImportEngine` runs.
- Or, on duplicate-key conflict error, automatically clean the target table (e.g. internal truncate/delete imported ranges) before resetting table mode to normal.
- Or, enforce an execution barrier/order so all secondary-index KV groups are fully validated/ingested before allowing data KV ingestion, plus a guaranteed cleanup path when any KV group fails.
entries.verify:
Add a realtikv regression covering a table with at least one `UNIQUE` secondary index:
1) Import a dataset with only unique-index conflicts (distinct PKs, duplicated unique key) using global sort and `on_duplicate_key='error'`.
2) Assert the statement errors with `[executor:8167]`.
3) After the task is cleaned up and table mode is normal, verify the table is either empty or fully consistent: run `ADMIN CHECK TABLE` and index-based queries that must not miss rows (or ensure automatic truncation happened).
entries.evidence:
- Default is strict: `pkg/executor/importer/import.go` sets `p.OnDupKey = OnDupKeyModeError` in `initDefaultOptions`, and `Plan.GetOnDupKeyMode()` maps empty -> `error`.
- Global-sort pipeline uses this mode to decide `engineapi.OnDuplicateKey{Record,Error}`: `pkg/dxf/importinto/encode_and_sort_operator.go` sets `SetOnDup(getOnDupForConflictedKV(op.onDupKey))` and index writers use `getOnDupForIndex(..., op.onDupKey)`; `pkg/dxf/importinto/task_executor.go` passes `ExternalEngineConfig.OnDup = onDup` then calls `ImportEngine`.
- Data/index KVs are ingested in different subtasks: `pkg/dxf/importinto/planner.go` comment says “data and index kv will NOT be in the same subtask” in `generateWriteIngestSpecs`.
- Subtask pick order is unspecified (no ordering): `pkg/dxf/framework/storage/task_table.go` `GetFirstSubtaskInStates` uses `... limit 1` without `ORDER BY`.
- Duplicate conflicts can surface in write+ingest (not only encode/merge): `tests/realtikvtest/importintotest4/conflict_resolution_test.go` has an “ingest-step” case where merge-sort is skipped and duplicates are detected when write+ingest loads KVs.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked history from this commit up to `upstream/master` (merge-base is this commit). No follow-up change was found that alters `on_duplicate_key` plumbing or adds ordering/rollback/auto-truncate for duplicate-key failures; `git log -S on_duplicate_key` shows no later edits to the core option handling. Later changes (e.g. table-mode reset timing) do not address KV-group partial-ingest consistency on duplicate errors.

entries.subject: planner: preserve outer refs in window subqueries (#66869)
entries.what: New window-subquery auxiliary-field discovery rewrites subquery expressions in a way that can execute uncorrelated scalar/EXISTS subqueries during planning, potentially causing double execution/side effects and semantic changes.
entries.impact: Queries with window expressions/specs that contain uncorrelated scalar or EXISTS subqueries can have those subqueries executed an extra time during planning (once in the new discovery pass, again during the real window arg/spec rewrite). This can cause user-visible side effects (e.g., sequence `nextval()`, locks, user-variable mutations), change nondeterministic results, and add extra executor work during optimization.
entries.fix: Avoid executing subqueries in the auxiliary-field discovery pass. Minimal approach: temporarily set `b.disableSubQueryPreprocessing = true` only around the `b.rewrite()` call(s) inside `appendAuxiliaryFieldsForSubqueries`, restoring it afterward, so discovery never triggers `EvalSubqueryFirstRow`. Alternative: plumb a dedicated “no-execution / correlated-cols-only” rewrite mode, or cache/reuse the later rewrite result so the subquery is rewritten at most once.
entries.verify: Add a regression test with a side-effectful uncorrelated scalar/EXISTS subquery inside a window expression/spec (e.g., using a sequence `nextval(seq)`), and assert the side effect happens exactly once. Also re-run the existing window subquery tests to ensure correlated outer-ref preservation still works.
entries.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go` adds `appendAuxiliaryFieldsForSubqueries()` and calls it from `resolveWindowFunction()`; it runs `b.rewrite(ctx, expr, p, nil, true)` on extracted subquery-bearing expressions just to discover correlated outer columns, discarding the rewritten expr/plan. `b.rewrite()` can execute *uncorrelated* scalar/EXISTS subqueries during optimization via `EvalSubqueryFirstRow` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go`, which calls into `pkg/executor/select.go` where `EvalSubqueryFirstRow` builds and runs an executor).

entries.subject: planner: support index join for embedded inner-join patterns (#66156)
entries.what: Data race / potential panic: enabling embedded inner-join patterns for index join causes concurrent inner-worker executor building to invoke the general `executorBuilder.build` (for the non-lookup child of an inner `PhysicalHashJoin`), which performs unsynchronized slice appends to shared `StmtCtx.TableIDs/IndexNames`.
entries.impact:
With `tidb_enable_inl_join_inner_multi_pattern=1` and an index join whose inner side contains an embedded `PhysicalHashJoin`, concurrent inner-worker builds can race on `StmtCtx.TableIDs/IndexNames`, leading to:
- potential slice corruption/panic in production,
- flaky behavior and `-race` test failures,
- incorrect statement summary/diagnostic metadata (even when it doesn’t crash).
entries.fix: When `executorBuilder.stmtCtxLock` is set (dataReaderBuilder/index-join inner workers), wrap all non-atomic `StmtCtx` mutations reachable from concurrent inner builds with `executorBuilder.withStmtCtxLock`, including the `StmtCtx.TableIDs` / `StmtCtx.IndexNames` appends in `buildTableReader`, `buildIndexLookUpReader`, `buildIndexMergeReader` (and audit other direct `StmtCtx` field writes).
entries.verify:
- Run race detector on index join paths that can build embedded inner hash joins, e.g. `go test -race ./pkg/executor/join -run TestIndex` and a query-level test enabling `tidb_enable_inl_join_inner_multi_pattern=1` with an embedded inner join under `INL_JOIN`.
- Specifically validate no concurrent writes to `StmtCtx.TableIDs/IndexNames` by running with `-race` while executing an index join where the inner plan contains a `PhysicalHashJoin` and the non-lookup child includes `TableReader`/`IndexLookUpReader`/`IndexMergeReader`.
entries.evidence:
- Index join inner workers are concurrent: `pkg/executor/join/index_lookup_join.go:197` spawns multiple `go innerWorker.run(...)` (`:209-213`), and each worker builds inner executors via `BuildExecutorForIndexJoin` (`pkg/executor/join/index_lookup_join.go:740-742`).
- This PR makes index-join inner plans support embedded hash joins: `dataReaderBuilder` handles `*physicalop.PhysicalHashJoin` (`pkg/executor/builder.go:5024-5025`) and, critically, builds the non-lookup side via the general builder (`pkg/executor/builder.go:5064`).
- General executor building mutates `StmtCtx.TableIDs/IndexNames` via unsynchronized slice appends, e.g.:
  - `pkg/executor/builder.go:4051` (`buildTableReader`: `sctx.TableIDs = append(...)`)
  - `pkg/executor/builder.go:4711-4712` (`buildIndexLookUpReader`: `sctx.IndexNames/TableIDs = append(...)`)
  - `pkg/executor/builder.go:4885-4899` (`buildIndexMergeReader`: `sctx.IndexNames/TableIDs = append(...)`)
- `StatementContext.TableIDs` and `IndexNames` are plain slices (`pkg/sessionctx/stmtctx/stmtctx.go:339-340`) with no internal synchronization, so concurrent appends are a data race.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: `git log b6af20e5..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/builder.go` shows only `44174cf474` and `319a683e05`, and `git diff b6af20e5..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/builder.go` does not add locking around the `StmtCtx.TableIDs/IndexNames` appends; `pkg/sessionctx/stmtctx/stmtctx.go` has no later changes either.

entries.subject: planner: enable index-only MV IndexMerge only for single covered partial path (optimizer part) (#66996)
entries.what: Plain `EXPLAIN` is made to output an index-only MV IndexMerge plan by constructing `PhysicalIndexMergeReader` with `TablePlan=nil`, but this plan is explicitly “not executable yet” and is blocked from being built/executed outside plain EXPLAIN. This creates an intentional divergence where `EXPLAIN` (non-analyze) can show a plan shape that the executor cannot run, and which will differ from actual execution and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`.
entries.impact: User-visible compatibility/diagnostics risk: plain `EXPLAIN` can show an index-only MV IndexMerge (no TableRowIDScan) that cannot be executed and will differ from both (a) actual query execution (which must still include a table scan) and (b) `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (where the EXPLAIN-only gate is disabled). This can mislead performance debugging and tooling that assumes `EXPLAIN` reflects the runnable plan.
entries.fix:
Avoid emitting non-executable physical plans in default `EXPLAIN` output:
- Preferred: implement executor support for index-only MV IndexMerge and remove the EXPLAIN-only gating so `EXPLAIN` and real execution share the same plan.
- If executor support isn’t ready: keep building a normal executable IndexMerge (with table scan) even in plain `EXPLAIN`, or make the hypothetical index-only shape opt-in via a session variable and/or clearly annotate the plan output as “not executable / planner-only”.
entries.verify:
- Compare `EXPLAIN FORMAT='plan_tree' ...` vs `EXPLAIN ANALYZE FORMAT='plan_tree' ...` for a single-partial-path MV IndexMerge query with covered projection; they should not diverge purely due to EXPLAIN mode.
- Ensure executing the query (non-EXPLAIN) never produces a plan requiring `buildIndexMergeReader` to hit the `len(TablePlans)==0` error path.
- If keeping any EXPLAIN-only behavior, add/adjust tests to assert the output is explicitly marked as non-executable/hypothetical.
entries.evidence:
- Planner side: `pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go:2231-2256` skips `BuildIndexMergeTableScan` when `canBuildSingleMVIndexOnlyIndexMerge` returns true, leaving `cop.TablePlan` nil (index-only IndexMerge for MV index).
- The gate is EXPLAIN-only and explicitly acknowledged as non-executable: `pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go:2281-2283` (“planner-only optimization… before executor support is added”, requires `StmtCtx.InExplainStmt && !InExplainAnalyzeStmt`).
